```diff
 ## Discover and install plugins
 
-You can browse and install plugins from marketplaces or directly from a Git repository.
-
-### Manage plugins with slash commands
-
-In a Copilot harness session, enter `/plugin ` in the chat input to view completions for plugin and marketplace operations.
-
-| Command | Purpose |
-|---------|---------|
-| `/plugin list` | List installed plugins and their status. |
-| `/plugin install <source>` | Install a plugin from a marketplace or Git repository. |
-| `/plugin update <plugin>` | Update an installed plugin. |
-| `/plugin enable <plugin>` | Enable an installed marketplace plugin. |
-| `/plugin disable <plugin>` | Disable an installed marketplace plugin. |
-| `/plugin uninstall <plugin>` | Remove an installed plugin. |
-| `/plugin marketplace list` | List included and registered marketplaces. |
-| `/plugin marketplace browse <name>` | Browse the plugins in a marketplace. |
-| `/plugin marketplace add <source>` | Add a marketplace from a Git repository. |
-| `/plugin marketplace update [name]` | Update one marketplace or all registered marketplaces. |
-| `/plugin marketplace remove <name> [--force]` | Remove a registered marketplace. Use `--force` if plugins from the marketplace are installed. |
-
-Marketplace plugins use the qualified identity `<plugin>@<marketplace>`. Use this identity when plugins in multiple marketplaces have the same name. Command completion suggests valid marketplace and plugin identities for each operation.
-
-Plugins installed directly from a Git repository can be updated or uninstalled, but they can't be enabled or disabled. To stop using a directly installed plugin, uninstall it. Included and centrally managed marketplaces can't be removed.
-
-> [!NOTE]
-> The `/plugin` commands and the Agent Customizations editor currently use separate plugin inventories. Manage a plugin from the interface where you installed it.

 ### Plugins installed by GitHub Copilot CLI
 
-VS Code automatically discovers plugins that you install with the [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/plugins-finding-installing) to enable you to use them also in VS Code. +VS Code automatically discovers plugins that you install with the [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/plugins-finding-installing) to enable you to use them also in VS Code. Discovered plugins from `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/` appear on the **Plugins** page of the Agent Customizations editor.
 
 The CLI stores plugins under `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>/`. Plugins installed directly from a Git URL (rather than from a marketplace) live under the `_direct` bucket, for example `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/_direct/github--moda-linter--copilot-plugin/`.
```

 Unlike [custom instructions](/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions.md) that primarily define coding guidelines, skills enable specialized capabilities and workflows that can include scripts, examples, and other resources. +## Use an existing skill
+
+Start with an existing skill when it provides the workflow you need. You can install a skill from a supported marketplace source, use one bundled in an [agent plugin](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md), or copy and adapt one for your project. Check [harness compatibility](/docs/agent-customization/overview.md#check-harness-compatibility) before choosing a source and location.
+
+A skill includes its full directory, not only the `SKILL.md` file: scripts, templates, examples, and other resources can be part of the workflow.
+
+### Install a skill from the Customization Marketplace (Preview)
+
+Use the Customization Marketplace to find and install skills from configured sources. Marketplace discovery is enabled by default. GitHub Feed requires a harness that provides marketplace search; Local sessions don't provide this source, and organization policy can restrict access.
+
+1. Open the Agent Customizations editor and select **Browse**.
+1. From the source menu, select **GitHub Feed**, and then search for a skill by name or add `@type:skill` to your search.
+1. Select a skill and review its publisher, source, and included files.
+1. Select **Install**, and choose a supported user or workspace destination when prompted.
+1. [Verify the installed skill](#verify-a-skill) in a session with the intended harness.
+
+VS Code doesn't overwrite an existing skill at the selected destination. If another supported location contains a skill with the same name, both skills appear on the **Skills** page. The source or publisher image identifies the Marketplace installation, and **Copy Relative Path** shows its exact location.
+
+VS Code tracks the directory of each skill installed from the Marketplace. Deleting that skill from the **Skills** page doesn't remove a local skill with the same name in another location.
+
+If files from a Marketplace-installed skill are missing, **Browse** shows **Missing files**. Select **Repair** to restore only the missing packaged files. Files that you changed or added remain unchanged.
+
+For more information about browsing sources and installation states, see [Discover marketplace customizations](/docs/agent-customization/overview.md#discover-marketplace-customizations-preview).
+
+### Copy and adapt an existing skill
+
+1. Review the skill's instructions, scripts, and other resources before adding it to your workspace.
+1. Copy the entire skill directory to a [supported project or personal location](#skill-locations) for your harness.
+1. Adapt the `SKILL.md` file to your needs. Check commands, file paths, dependencies, and assumptions about the project.
+1. Update any supporting scripts, templates, or examples that the adapted instructions use.
+1. [Verify the adapted skill](#verify-a-skill) before sharing it.
+
+> [!TIP]
+> Only reuse skills you trust. Skills can include scripts that run tools or interact with external systems. Review [security considerations](/docs/agents/run/security.md#approvals-and-review) before using them.
+

```diff
+### Edit a custom agent file
+
+Use completions and hover details in an `.agent.md` file to choose values for the intended harness. By default, editing follows the selected harness. An explicit `target` overrides how the editor interprets the file, but doesn't switch your session's harness. See [Harness compatibility](/docs/agents/reference/custom-agent-file-reference.md#harness-compatibility).
+
+For Copilot-assisted editing, set `target` explicitly when you need target-specific guidance. Without an explicit target, the file context supplied to Copilot describes only shared attributes and doesn't suggest target-specific model or tool values. This differs from normal editor completions, which follow the selected harness.
+
+Hover a value to inspect its details or availability. The editor refreshes validation as harness inventories change. Unknown-value hints depend on discovery completing, so the absence of a hint while discovery is pending doesn't confirm that a value is available.
+
+Select the intended harness before editing, then try the agent in that harness to verify its behavior. Editor feedback doesn't replace checking which tools and skills the running agent can use.
+
 ## Use a custom agent
 
 Select the intended harness from the **Session Target** UI control, then choose your custom agent from the **Agent** dropdown in chat. Enter a prompt for its role and review the response and tool calls. The custom agent remains selected until you switch agents.
```

```diff
 Add an MCP server when your agent needs a capability its existing tools don't provide, such as querying a database or retrieving information from an external service. [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) connects agents to these tools and data sources. If your existing tools meet your needs, you don't need another server.
 
+For supported services, [Copilot connectors](/docs/agent-customization/copilot-connectors.md) `feature(copilot-connectors)` provide [product.prodname_github]-managed MCP connections for Copilot harness sessions without local server setup or manual MCP configuration.
+
 This article takes you from adding a server to verifying its first tool call. Choose your starting point:
 
+* **Connect a supported service without server setup:** [Use a Copilot connector](/docs/agent-customization/copilot-connectors.md) `feature(copilot-connectors)`.
+* **Use tools from a packaged workflow:** [Install an agent plugin](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md#discover-and-install-plugins) that bundles MCP servers.
 * **I have a server URL or command:** [Connect a server](#connect-a-server).
 * **Help me find a server:** [Choose a server to try](#choose-a-server-to-try).
 * **My server is configured but isn't working:** [Check the connection](#if-the-server-does-not-work).
```

```diff
+## Choose how to access models
+
+Start with the account, credentials, or model you already have:
+
+* **GitHub Copilot access**: [Set up Copilot](/docs/setup/copilot.md), then [choose a model](#change-the-model-for-chat) from the providers available through your plan.
+* **A provider account or harness-specific credentials**: Follow the [[product.prodname_anthropic_claude]](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#claude) or [[product.prodname_openai_codex]](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#codex) requirements for that harness. Supported accounts and authentication methods depend on the integration.
+* **An API key or custom endpoint**: [Add a model provider](#bring-your-own-language-model-key) in the Language Models editor. This configures model access, not a different harness.
+* **A locally running model**: Add a [model provider extension](#add-a-model-provider-extension), such as Ollama. Alternatively, check the hardware and sign-in requirements for [Copilot-managed on-device models](#on-device-model-requirements).
+
+The model provides reasoning, the harness coordinates tools and workflow, and the access provider determines authentication and billing. These choices are related, but aren't interchangeable. Compare [harness-specific access options](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#requirements-and-setup) before reusing an account or key.
+

+### Organization-managed model defaults
+
+Your organization can set the starting model for new conversations in both the editor and the Agents window. The model picker marks the organization's choice as **Org default**, and the Settings editor shows an indicator for ``chat.defaultModel`` with a **Managed by organization** explanation.
+
+The managed default takes precedence over your saved model preference for new conversations, but you can still select another available model for the current conversation. Existing conversations keep their model. Your saved preference is preserved and applies to new conversations again when the managed default is removed.
+
+For administrator configuration, see [Set managed model defaults](/docs/enterprise/manage-ai-settings.md#set-managed-model-defaults).
+
+## Configure thinking effort and context size
+
+Some models support configurable thinking effort, context size, and other parameters.These control how much reasoning the model applies to each request, and how much context the model can consider at once. For background on thinking and reasoning, see [Thinking and reasoning](/docs/agents/concepts/language-models.md#thinking-and-reasoning).
+
+By default, VS Code sets recommended effort levels and has adaptive reasoning enabled, where the model dynamically determines how much to think based on the complexity of each request. For most use cases, the default configuration works well.
 
 > [!TIP]
 > Higher thinking effort produces more thinking tokens, which increases [AI credit](/docs/agents/concepts/language-models.md#ai-credits-and-model-costs) consumption. Only increase thinking effort for genuinely complex tasks. Learn more about [optimizing AI credit usage](/docs/agents/guides/optimize-usage.md).

+
+Copilot Fusion chooses models and a workflow to complete your task, so you don't need to select a model for each step. For background on how Fusion differs from Auto and when to use it, see [Copilot Fusion concepts](/docs/agents/concepts/language-models.md#copilot-fusion).

+1. In the model picker, select **Copilot Fusion**, then choose an available tier: **Standard**, **High**, or **Max**.
```

```diff
+## Choose how to customize
+
+Start with a recurring task or an observed problem. You don't need to create every customization yourself, or add one when the agent already meets your needs.
+
+### Install or reuse
+
+Use an existing customization when it provides the workflow or capability you need:
+
+* **[Install an agent plugin](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md#discover-and-install-plugins)**: Add related skills, agents, and tool integrations together.
+* **[Use an existing skill](/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills.md#use-an-existing-skill)**: Reuse its instructions, scripts, and resources for your task.
+* **Connect an external system**: [Use a Copilot connector](/docs/agent-customization/copilot-connectors.md) `feature(copilot-connectors)` without server setup, or [add an MCP server](/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers.md#connect-a-server) using a URL or launch command.
+
+For supported marketplace sources, you can also [browse customizations in the editor](#discover-marketplace-customizations-preview) (Preview). Review the publisher, included files, and setup requirements before installing or running a customization.
+
+### Create or adapt
+
+Adapt existing instructions or a skill when they nearly match your needs. Create a new customization when you need project-specific guidance or a workflow that isn't already available.
+
+Follow [Configure AI for your codebase](/docs/agents/guides/customize-copilot-guide.md) to add a customization and compare the agent's results before and after the change. To create an individual customization with AI or manually, use the [creation steps below](#create-a-customization).
+
+You can combine these approaches: install a plugin, then add project instructions for your codebase.
+
 ## Check harness compatibility
```

```diff
 ### Memory
 
-When the memory tool is available, an agent can store notes for use later in the same session or in future sessions. These notes can record preferences, lessons from previous tasks, or information about your codebase. Memory is separate from the conversation context that a session accumulates automatically.
+Memory retains preferences and codebase knowledge separately from the conversation context that a session accumulates automatically. The memory system depends on the agent harness:
 
-The memory tool stores notes locally on your machine in three scopes:
-
-* **User memory** (`/memories/`): persists across all workspaces and conversations. The first 200 lines are automatically loaded into every session.
-* **Repository memory** (`/memories/repo/`): scoped to the current workspace and persists across conversations.
-* **Session memory** (`/memories/session/`): scoped to the current conversation and cleared when it ends.
+* **[copilot.copilot_memory]**: Sessions that use the Copilot harness locally can recall cloud-backed repository facts and user preferences. Repository facts are shared with people who have access to that repository and memory. User preferences apply to your own supported interactions across repositories.
+* **File-based memory**: The Local harness uses a separate memory tool for user, repository, and session notes. These files are stored locally by default. Session memory can hold temporary task context, such as an implementation plan.
 
 Learn more about [memory in VS Code agents](/docs/agents/run/memory.md).
 
```

```diff
--- microsoft_vscode-docs::docs/agents/concepts/tools.md (prev: 31225c07)
+++ microsoft_vscode-docs::docs/agents/concepts/tools.md (new: 02e1c511)
@@ -25,8 +25,18 @@
 VS Code supports three types of tools:
 
 * **Built-in tools**: tools that ship with VS Code for common development tasks, like reading and writing files, running terminal commands, searching your codebase, and navigating the editor. These are available immediately without any setup.
-* **MCP tools**: tools provided by [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) servers, an open standard for connecting AI models to external tools and data sources. MCP servers can run locally on your machine or be hosted remotely. Use MCP tools to connect to databases, APIs, and other external services.
+* **MCP tools**: tools provided by [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) servers, an open standard for connecting AI models to external tools and data sources. MCP tools can come from servers you [configure directly](/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers.md), managed [Copilot connectors](/docs/agent-customization/copilot-connectors.md) `feature(copilot-connectors)`, or servers bundled in [agent plugins](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md). MCP servers can run locally on your machine or be hosted remotely. Use MCP tools to connect to databases, APIs, and other external services.
 * **Extension tools**: tools contributed by VS Code extensions through the Language Model Tools API. Extension tools integrate deeply with the editor and are available when you install the extension.
+
+### Connect external services
+
+[Copilot connectors](/docs/agent-customization/copilot-connectors.md) `feature(copilot-connectors)` are [product.prodname_github]-managed connections that add MCP tools to your agent. For example, connect Microsoft Learn Docs so the agent can retrieve official documentation while working on a task.
+
+Use a connector for a supported service when you want a managed connection without local server setup or manual MCP configuration. If the service isn't available as a connector or you need a custom integration, [add an MCP server](/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers.md).
+
+Connectors are available in Copilot harness sessions, not Local sessions. [Connect a service from the Agent Customizations editor](/docs/agent-customization/copilot-connectors.md#connect-a-service).
+
+[Agent plugins](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md) can bundle MCP servers with skills, custom agents, and other customizations. Use a plugin when you want those tools as part of a packaged workflow.
 
 ## How agents choose tools
 
@@ -36,7 +46,7 @@
 
 ## Control which tools are available
 
-An available tool comes from VS Code, an MCP server, or an installed extension. An enabled tool is one that the agent is permitted to choose for a request.
+An available tool comes from VS Code, an installed extension, or an MCP server. To add MCP tools, configure a server, connect a Copilot connector, or install an agent plugin that bundles a server. An enabled tool is one that the agent is permitted to choose for a request.
 
 Limit enabled tools to the capabilities that are relevant to your task. A focused set helps the agent choose appropriate tools, reduces the chance of unnecessary actions, and limits the tool output added to the [context window](/docs/agents/concepts/language-models.md#context-window).
 
```

```diff
@@ -16,7 +16,7 @@
 Agents can read files, edit code, run terminal commands, and call external services. VS Code's trust model layers several control mechanisms so you remain in charge of what reaches your codebase:
 
 * **Review before integrating.** Agents can save edits directly in the session folder or worktree. Inspect the changes in a diff before you commit, merge, or create a pull request. For supported sessions, [checkpoints](/docs/agents/run/review-code-edits.md#edit-requests-and-restore-checkpoints) restore affected workspace files and chat to an earlier point.
-* **Approve sensitive actions.** With [Manual permissions](/docs/agents/run/approvals.md#permission-levels) in Copilot harness sessions, actions that aren't covered by your approval settings require confirmation. File edits might be auto-approved. Configure [sensitive-file approval](/docs/agents/run/review-code-edits.md#edit-sensitive-files) when an edit must require confirmation before it is applied.
+* **Approve sensitive actions.** With [Manual permissions](/docs/agents/run/approvals.md#permission-levels) in Copilot harness sessions, actions that aren't covered by your approval settings require confirmation. File edits might be auto-approved. Configure [sensitive-file approval](/docs/agents/run/review-code-edits.md#require-approval-before-sensitive-edits) when an edit must require confirmation before it is applied.
 * **Constrain autonomy.** [Permission levels](/docs/agents/run/approvals.md#permission-levels) decide how much the agent runs on its own, from per-call approvals to broad auto-approval, up to fully autonomous operation with Autopilot.
 * **Enforce boundaries at the OS level.** [Agent sandboxing](#agent-sandboxing) restricts file system and network access for terminal commands so auto-approved actions cannot escape a defined scope.
 * **Trust boundaries.** VS Code uses trust decisions for workspaces, extensions, MCP servers, and network domains. Workspace MCP servers inherit Workspace Trust.
@@ -35,6 +35,8 @@
 * **Network domain**: controls whether the agent can fetch content from a URL. VS Code prompts you to trust a domain before making requests to it, integrated with the [Trusted Domains](/docs/editing/editingevolved.md#outgoing-link-protection) list. You can also enable ``chat.agent.networkFilter`` to restrict domains for the fetch tool and integrated browser. [Sandbox network controls](/docs/agents/run/agent-sandboxing.md#configure-network-access) apply separately to terminal commands.
 
 You can revoke trust at any time through dedicated commands in the Command Palette. Changing Workspace Trust controls whether workspace MCP servers can run. For servers with a separate trust decision, run **MCP: Reset Trust**. For steps to configure these controls, see [AI security in VS Code](/docs/agents/run/security.md).
+
+Authorizing a [Copilot connector](/docs/agent-customization/copilot-connectors.md) `feature(copilot-connectors)` grants access to the connected service. This is separate from approval of individual tool calls. The session's permission and approval settings still determine whether a tool action requires confirmation.
 
 ## Agent sandboxing

It does not add domain filtering to Copilot's built-in shell or the Windows terminal sandbox. See [sandbox network capabilities](/docs/agents/run/agent-sandboxing.md#configure-network-access).
 
-Use the [review flow](/docs/agents/run/review-code-edits.md) and [sensitive file protection](/docs/agents/run/review-code-edits.md#edit-sensitive-files) to control these operations.
+Use the [review flow](/docs/agents/run/review-code-edits.md) and [sensitive file protection](/docs/agents/run/review-code-edits.md#require-approval-before-sensitive-edits) to control these operations.
 
 A [Dev Container session](/docs/agents/run/agents-window.md#run-a-session-in-a-dev-container) runs the agent and its workspace tools inside the project's container, on your machine or a supported connected host. This is different from a Git worktree, which separates code changes, and terminal sandboxing, which restricts command access.
```

```diff
 ![Screenshot of the Language Models editor, showing the list of available models.](../images/language-models/language-models-editor.png)
 
@@ -68,7 +68,9 @@
 
 ### Auto model selection
 
-Auto model selection in GitHub Copilot combines two systems to route each request to the optimal model. One system tracks real-time model health and availability, while the other evaluates task complexity. Together, they match each task to the model that can solve it most efficiently, reserving higher-cost reasoning models for problems that need them and routing simpler tasks to faster models.
+Auto model selection in GitHub Copilot combines two systems to select one model for each request. One system tracks real-time model health and availability, while the other evaluates task complexity. Together, they match each task to the model that can solve it most efficiently, reserving higher-cost reasoning models for problems that need them and routing simpler tasks to faster models.
+
+In [Copilot harness sessions](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#copilot), the same routing entry can appear as **Copilot Fusion** instead of **Auto**, depending on your settings and the tiers offered to your account. Fusion adds [multi-model orchestration](#copilot-fusion) alongside single-model routing.
 
 Auto selects from multiple models and respects your organization's [model access settings](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-ai-models/configure-access-to-ai-models). Auto won't select models excluded by administrator policies or models restricted by data-residency policies.
 
@@ -76,9 +78,19 @@
 
 For more details, see [About Copilot auto model selection](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/auto-model-selection) in the GitHub documentation.
 
+### Copilot Fusion
+
+Copilot Fusion is a model orchestration system, not an individual language model. It chooses models and a workflow for your task, so you don't need to coordinate each step yourself. Unlike Auto, which selects one model per request, Fusion can use one model or coordinate multiple models. For example, one model can draft a solution, another can critique it, and the original model can revise it. You receive a single final response.
+
+Consider Fusion for substantial, well-scoped coding tasks where additional review can be worth the extra time and [AI credits](#ai-credits-and-model-costs). Availability depends on your account and organization policies.
+
+Learn how to [use Copilot Fusion](/docs/agent-customization/language-models.md#use-copilot-fusion). For details about orchestration, see [Copilot model orchestration](https://docs.github.com/en/early-access/copilot/hydrafusion) in the GitHub documentation.
+
 ### AI credits and model costs
 
 Each Copilot plan includes a monthly allowance of [AI credits](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/billing/usage-based-billing-for-individuals). Different models consume AI credits at different rates, based on the model and the number of tokens processed. More capable models cost more per token, while lighter models extend your usage further. When you use auto model selection, VS Code routes each request to an efficient model that balances quality and cost.
+
+Copilot Fusion can use multiple model passes for a task, such as drafting, critique, and revision. Each pass contributes to AI credit consumption, so an orchestrated workflow can take longer and use more credits than a single-model request.
 
 Other factors also affect credit consumption, such as [thinking effort](/docs/agent-customization/language-models.md#configure-thinking-effort) (higher effort produces more thinking tokens), context window size, and tool usage. Prompt caching lowers the effective cost of a request by reusing tokens from a previous one. You can inspect cache hit rates with the [Cache Explorer](/docs/agents/agent-troubleshooting/cache-explorer.md). For practical tips on reducing credit consumption, see [optimize AI credit usage](/docs/agents/guides/optimize-usage.md).
 
```

```diff
 > [!CAUTION]
 > Worktrees isolate working files, not the agent's access to your machine or external services. Copilot worktree sessions use **Allow all**, which skips tool approval prompts. Use a trusted repository and review the [permission and sandboxing controls](/docs/agents/run/approvals.md) before proceeding. If you require manual approvals, use folder sessions one at a time instead.
```

```diff
-**MetaDescription**: Explore AI in Visual Studio Code, from code suggestions to agents that plan, edit, and test changes.
+**MetaDescription**: Choose AI workflows, models, and agents in VS Code, from inline suggestions to remote sessions.
 
 # Build with AI in VS Code
 
-Use AI in Visual Studio Code to understand unfamiliar code, fix bugs, and build features. For a task that spans files and tools, an agent can find relevant code, make changes, and run checks without you directing each search, edit, and test run. You describe the outcome, review the changes, and verify the result.
+Use as much or as little AI as your task needs in Visual Studio Code. Get suggestions as you type, collaborate with an agent beside your code, or coordinate tasks across projects in the Agents window. Combine these approaches as your work changes.
 
-Work with an agent in the same workspace as your editor, terminal, tests, and debugger. You can inspect its changes and investigate failures without moving code and command output to a separate chat application. For a question or focused edit, use chat, inline chat, or suggestions without delegating an entire task.
+You can choose models from multiple providers and work with the Copilot, Claude, or Codex agent harness, using a supported account or your own API key. Customizations and plugins help you tailor agents to your work.
 
-For day-to-day coding and agent tasks, start with the [Copilot harness](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#copilot) to explore code, plan changes, implement features, and run tests. The harness uses a shared runtime for core capabilities and more consistent behavior across VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, and the GitHub Copilot app. You can continue the same live session in the Chat view or Agents window, and [discover and continue supported sessions created in GitHub Copilot CLI or the GitHub Copilot app](/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions.md#view-sessions-from-other-applications).
+Continuity lets you pick up agent work across supported interfaces without starting over. Connect to sessions on your own machine through GitHub Environments, or use a cloud session without keeping a local host online.
 
-Choose another [agent harness](/docs/agents/concepts/agent-harnesses.md) when you need its tools or workflows, or delegate an independent task to a [cloud agent](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#start-a-cloud-session).
+## Try your first agent task
 
-<div class="docs-action" data-show-in-doc="true" data-show-in-sidebar="false" title="Try your first agent task">
-Build and validate a small app in the Chat view, then review the result.

+* **New to VS Code:** First [install the editor and open a workspace](/docs/getstarted/overview.md).

+## Choose how you work
+

-If you're new to both VS Code and AI, first [install the editor and open a workspace](/docs/getstarted/overview.md). If you already use agents, skip the sample project and follow the [experienced-agent fast track](/docs/agents/guides/overview.md#experienced-agent-fast-track). For AI help without delegating a task, [choose between suggestions, focused edits, questions, and agents](/docs/agents/reference/ai-features-cheat-sheet.md#choose-a-feature).
+An [agent](/docs/agents/concepts/agents.md) uses a model and tools to find relevant code, make changes, and run checks. Both the Chat view and the Agents window run agents. You set the goal, guide the work, and review the results.
 
-The quickstart uses the [GitHub Copilot harness](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#copilot). See the [Copilot setup guide](/docs/setup/copilot.md) for account, usage, and data-handling requirements. If provider, sign-in, or execution location affects your setup, [compare agent harnesses](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#compare-agent-harnesses) and review their [requirements and setup](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#requirements-and-setup).
+For routine work, save a prompt as an [automation](/docs/agents/run/automations.md). Run it locally on a schedule, or use cloud automations `feature(cloud-automations)` for scheduled or event-triggered repository work that continues while your computer is off. Review a manual run before enabling recurring work.
 
-## What you can do with AI
-
-Choose a workflow based on the task, from help with a single line to a coordinated change across your project.
-
-| Your goal | How AI helps |
-|-----------|--------------|
-| Implement a feature, fix a bug, or refactor across files | [Work with an agent](#how-you-work-with-an-agent) to find relevant code, make changes, and run tests. |
-| Understand a codebase or explore an approach | [Ask questions in chat](/docs/chat/chat-overview.md) to get explanations grounded in your code and discuss alternatives. |
-| Research a complex change before editing | [Plan with an agent](/docs/agents/run/planning.md) and review the proposed approach before implementation. |
-| Make a focused edit without leaving your code | Use [inline chat](/docs/chat/inline-chat.md) to describe the change in the editor. |
-| Get code suggestions while you type | Use [inline suggestions](/docs/editing/ai-powered-suggestions.md) for completions and suggested next edits. |
-| Complete a common development task | Use [smart actions](/docs/editing/copilot-smart-actions.md) for tasks such as generating a commit message or explaining selected code. |
-
-You use chat both to ask questions and to direct agents. You can ask **Agent** to propose an approach before editing, or select **Plan**, where available, for a dedicated planning workflow.
-
-For a compact comparison, use the [AI features cheat sheet](/docs/agents/reference/ai-features-cheat-sheet.md#choose-a-feature) to choose the least autonomous option that fits your task.
-
-## How you work with an agent
-
-An agent uses a language model to reason about your request and [tools](/docs/agents/concepts/tools.md) to act on your development environment. It gathers [context](/docs/agents/concepts/context.md), such as code, error messages, and test results, rather than relying only on the words in your prompt.
-
-For example, ask an agent to fix a failing test while preserving the intended behavior:
-
-1. The agent finds the test and reads the related code to understand the failure.
-1. It edits the implementation or tests based on the task and your constraints.
-1. It runs the tests, inspects the results, and revises its changes if needed.
-1. You review the diff and validation results, verify the behavior yourself, and decide which changes to keep.
-
-This repeated reasoning, action, and validation is the **agent loop**. You can provide more context, redirect the work, or stop the agent along the way. Learn more about [how agents work](/docs/agents/concepts/agents.md).
-
-The conversation and work for a task belong to a **session**. Sessions keep related context and changes together so you can return to a task or manage independent tasks separately. Learn about [sessions and handoff](/docs/agents/concepts/sessions.md).
-
-## Ways to work with agents
-
-Both the Chat view and the Agents window support agent workflows. Choose the Chat view for collaboration over code in your current workspace, or the Agents window for multi-project orchestration and higher-level task assignment. You can continue supported sessions between them rather than choosing one interface for every task.
-
-For a path from your first request through planning, steering, review, and recovery, see [Run agents in VS Code](/docs/agents/run/overview.md).
-
-### Work alongside your code
-
-Use the [Chat view](/docs/agents/run/chat-view.md) when you're working in an open project. Keep the conversation beside your editor, inspect changes as they happen, and use the debugger, terminal, and tests as part of the same workflow. This is the starting point for the agents quickstart.
-
-![Screenshot showing the Chat view with the sessions list, conversation, and chat input.](images/agents-overview/chat-view-expanded.png)
-
-For keyboard, screen reader, and low-vision workflows, learn how to use the [Accessible View and other accessibility features](/docs/configure/accessibility/accessibility.md#accessible-view).
-
-### Delegate and manage tasks
-
-Use the [Agents window](/docs/agents/run/agents-window.md) when your focus is assigning tasks and reviewing their results. Manage multiple sessions across projects, follow their progress, and open the editor when you want to work directly with the code.
-
-![Screenshot showing how to start a new agent session by selecting New at the top of the sidebar in the Agents window.](images/agents-overview/agents-window-hero.png)
-
-### Other ways to access agents
-
-For terminal-based work, use [GitHub Copilot CLI](/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions.md#use-copilot-cli-from-the-terminal). The [GitHub Copilot app](https://github.com/features/copilot) provides a dedicated desktop experience. You can [open and continue supported local sessions created in either application](/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions.md#view-sessions-from-other-applications) in VS Code. To continue a Copilot session in the CLI, right-click the session and select **Resume in Terminal**.
```

```diff
-Hooks in a plugin-provided custom agent's frontmatter have a separate [conversion limitation](/docs/agent-customization/hooks.md#agent-scoped-hooks): VS Code currently omits the agent's `hooks` field when passing that agent to the Copilot harness. +Hooks in a plugin-provided custom agent's frontmatter are [scoped to that agent](/docs/agent-customization/hooks.md#agent-scoped-hooks). VS Code forwards those hooks when passing the agent to Copilot. The agent appearing in the picker doesn't prove its hooks run, so verify the expected events and decisions in a trusted session. Keep agent-specific hooks in the agent's frontmatter rather than broadening them to plugin-wide execution.
 
 ### How plugin hooks interact with other hooks
 
 Plugin-wide hooks run alongside other applicable hook sources. For Copilot `preToolUse`, a denial blocks the tool call. Return no decision when the hook should leave the normal permission flow unchanged. Review the runtime's timeout and failure rules before relying on a hook for validation.
 
-Disabling a plugin also disables its hooks. Unless enterprise policy controls the plugin's enablement, you can enable or disable plugins globally or for a specific workspace from the Extensions view.
+Disabling a plugin also disables its hooks. Unless enterprise policy controls the plugin's enablement, you can [enable or disable plugins](/docs/agent-customization/agent-plugins.md#enable-or-disable-plugins) for the current profile or a specific workspace from the Agent Customizations editor.
```

+Use the model identifiers inserted by completions for the intended harness. Copilot completions insert runtime model IDs, including exact provider-qualified IDs for BYOK models. These differ from Local's qualified model display names.
+
+To specify a prioritized list for Copilot, replace the placeholders with available model IDs. Keep the array in your preferred order:
+
+```yaml
+model: ['<preferred model ID>', '<fallback model ID>']
+```
+
+The Copilot editor schema also recognizes `model-policy: preferred` and `model-policy: required`. Conversion of plugin-provided agents selects a model from the authored list but doesn't forward `model-policy`. Don't rely on `required` to enforce a required-model policy for those converted agents.
+
+### Skills
+
+In Copilot, use `skills` to name skills to load into the custom agent's context:
+
+```yaml
+skills: ['<skill name>']
+```
+
+Replace `<skill name>` with an enabled skill available to the intended Copilot harness. Completions and hovers show descriptions, sources, and availability details where provided. Disabled or temporarily unavailable skills can also appear, so review their status before selecting them.
+
+This inventory validation is specific to Copilot files. Setting `target: vscode` uses Local interpretation instead. For skill creation and supported locations, see [Agent skills](/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills.md).
+
+### Copilot-specific configuration
+
+The editor provides nested completions, hovers, and structural validation for these Copilot fields:
+
+* `github`: a `toolsets` array and a `permissions` map. GitHub MCP toolsets aren't Local user-defined tool-set files.
+* `mcp-servers`: a map of server definitions, with local command-based or remote URL-based configurations. The editor checks property types, tool arrays, URLs, and positive timeouts.
+* `hooks`: event maps with action arrays. Validation checks event-specific action combinations, matcher patterns, URLs, and positive timeouts. Use the [agent-scoped hook reference](/docs/agent-customization/hooks.md#agent-scoped-hooks) for runtime requirements.
+
+Structural validation doesn't start or authenticate MCP servers, or prove that a hook executes.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Editor schema support doesn't guarantee runtime support. When converting agent files to SDK custom-agent configuration, including plugin-provided agents, VS Code doesn't forward `model-policy`, `mcp-servers`, `github`, `deferred-tool-loading`, `strict-tools-list`, or `include-custom-instructions`. Don't rely on those fields to configure the runtime behavior of converted agents. To make MCP tools available to a session, use the [supported MCP server configuration](/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers.md).

 ## Adjust the window layout
 
+### Arrange chat tabs and groups
+
+For sessions that support [multiple chats](/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions.md#run-multiple-chats-in-a-session), use ``sessions.showChatTabs`` to choose how conversations appear:
+
+* **Multiple**: Show each open chat as a tab, with optional split groups.
+* **Single**: Show the active chat as the session view. Selecting a nested session replaces the unpinned chat pane. A chat explicitly opened to the side stays visible, and closing the last nested session pane doesn't reopen the main chat.
+
+In **Multiple**, arrange chat groups with the mouse or keyboard:
+
+* Drag a tab to the center of another group to move it there.
+* Drag a tab to a group's left, right, top, or bottom edge to create a group in that direction.
+* Run **Sessions: Split Chat Group Right**, **Sessions: Split Chat Group Down**, **Sessions: Move Chat to Previous Group**, or **Sessions: Move Chat to Next Group** from the Command Palette (``Shortcut: workbench.action.showCommands``).
+* Press ``Shortcut: sessions.focusPreviousChatGroup`` or ``Shortcut: sessions.focusNextChatGroup`` to move focus between groups.
+
+Moving or closing the last chat in a group closes that group and expands the remaining groups. Visible and hidden chats, their history, group assignments, active chats, and split sizes are restored when you switch sessions or reload the window.
+
+To arrange separate top-level sessions instead, see [Arrange sessions in a grid](/docs/agents/run/agents-window.md#arrange-sessions-in-a-grid).
+
+To hide the sessions sidebar, select **Toggle Sidebar** in the top-left corner or press ``Shortcut: workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility``.
+
 ### Use the single-pane editor panel (Experimental)
 
 The experimental single-pane layout replaces the separate editor and side panel with one docked pane. A shared tab bar spans the editor and the **Changes** or **Files** detail view. Files and diffs open in the docked editor next to the chat instead of in a modal window.

```diff
+## Start an agent session
+
+If this is your first agent task, follow the [agents quickstart](/docs/agents/quickstart.md) for a complete example with recommended settings. For work in your own project, choose a task with a clear outcome and checks you can run to verify it.
+
+Start a session for a local folder, GitHub repository, or [remote workspace](/docs/agents/run/remote-agent-sessions.md). You can attach other projects, issues, and pull requests as context before you send the first prompt. For work that doesn't belong to a project, start a [quick chat](#start-a-quick-chat).
+
+To connect to and organize remote machines in one place, use [remote environment management (Experimental)](/docs/agents/run/remote-agent-sessions.md#manage-remote-environments-experimental).
+
+For interactive work on managed compute, [start a cloud session](/docs/agents/run/cloud-sandbox-sessions.md#start-a-cloud-session) `feature(cloud-sessions)`. The cloud environment runs the task independently of your local machine. To continue it later, [reopen the existing session](/docs/agents/run/cloud-sandbox-sessions.md#continue-an-existing-cloud-session) rather than starting another task.
+
+To start a new agent session in the Agents window:
+
+1. Select **New** at the top of the sidebar or press ``Shortcut: workbench.action.chat.newChat``. To start directly in a specific workspace, hover over the workspace in the sessions list and select **+** (New Session).
+
+1. Select **Folder** or **Repository** to choose the primary execution workspace for the session. The first folder or repository you select determines where the agent runs and changes files.
+
+    To connect through SSH or a dev tunnel, select **Remote Setup**. If the workspace isn't trusted, review the [Workspace Trust](/docs/editing/workspaces/workspace-trust.md) prompt before you continue.
+
+1. Optionally, attach more context to the request:
+
+    * Select **Folder** or **Repository** to attach more projects as context without adding workspace roots.
+    * Select **Add Context**, and then select **Issue...** or **Pull Request...**. If multiple GitHub repositories are available, select a repository before you choose the issue or pull request.
+    * Paste a GitHub issue or pull request URL directly into the prompt. The URL remains in the prompt, and VS Code automatically adds the item as a context attachment.
+
+    ![Screenshot of the new-session input highlighting the folder name and the Create PR control.](../images/agents-window/new-session-input.png)
+
+1. Choose an available agent harness, and optionally configure the agent, language model, permission level, and isolation mode. For folder isolation in a local Git repository, you can also select an existing local branch to check out before the session starts. The available options depend on the workspace. Learn how to [compare agent harnesses](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#compare-agent-harnesses) and [choose where the agent makes changes](#choose-where-an-agent-makes-changes).
+
+1. Type a prompt that describes what you want to accomplish, and press ``Enter`` to submit it to the agent.
+
+    > [!TIP]
+    > To start a session in the background without leaving the current session, press ``Alt+Enter`` or hold ``Alt`` and select **Send**. The new session appears in the sessions list after you send the prompt.
+
+The sessions list shows the session's status and change statistics while it works. Review questions and approval requests as they appear, then [review and validate the result](#review-and-finish-an-agent-session) before integrating changes. For shared conversation controls, including how to steer or stop a request, see [Use chat](/docs/chat/chat-overview.md).
+
+### Choose where an agent makes changes
+
+For a workspace session in the Agents window, choose whether the agent edits your current folder or works in a separate [Git worktree](/docs/sourcecontrol/branches-worktrees.md#understanding-worktrees). Use a worktree to keep an agent's changes separate from your active workspace, especially when you run tasks in parallel.
+
+Code isolation controls where the agent applies file changes. The permission level controls which actions require your approval. A worktree keeps changes out of your active workspace, but it does not restrict commands, network access, or access to files outside the worktree.
+
+| Choice | Choose it for | Considerations |
+|--------|---------------|----------------|
+| **New Worktree** | Parallel tasks that should not modify your active workspace | Starts from committed Git state and requires you to integrate the result |
+| **Folder** | Small, interactive tasks that should use your current files and uncommitted changes | Agent edits appear immediately in your active workspace |
+
+For a walkthrough with separate worktrees for two independent tasks, follow [Delegate two tasks without mixing their changes](/docs/agents/guides/delegate-two-tasks.md).
+
+When you [start a session](#start-an-agent-session), select **New Worktree** and choose the base branch. The base branch provides the initial contents of the new worktree and does not change the branch in your active workspace.
+
+If you leave **New Worktree** unselected, the agent works directly in the selected folder. For a local Git repository with at least one branch, you can select an existing local branch to check out before the agent starts. Checking out a branch changes the branch in your active workspace and requires a clean working tree. Commit or stash your changes before you select another branch. The branch selection is not remembered for later sessions.
+
+Sessions that you start in the Chat view always use the current workspace. **Local** sessions also always apply changes in the active workspace.
+
+In VS Code Insiders, ``sessions.useWorktree`` controls whether **New Worktree** is selected when you create your first workspace session. After you start a session, VS Code remembers your isolation choice across workspaces and uses it instead of this setting.
+
+![Screenshot showing the New Worktree checkbox and base branch control in the Agents window.](../images/agent-harnesses/agents-window-new-worktree.png)
+
+Worktree isolation requires a Git repository with at least one commit. A new worktree contains the committed files from the selected base branch. It does not automatically contain uncommitted tracked changes or untracked files from your primary worktree. Commit changes that the agent needs, or use folder isolation when the task depends on your current uncommitted state.
+
+Git-ignored files, such as `.env` files and installed dependencies, are also absent by default. Use ``git.worktreeIncludeFiles`` to [copy ignored files into new worktrees](/docs/sourcecontrol/branches-worktrees.md#include-files-when-creating-a-worktree). For large ignored folders, ``git.worktreeSymlinkFolders`` (Experimental) can [symlink a folder instead](/docs/sourcecontrol/branches-worktrees.md#symlink-ignored-folders-when-creating-a-worktree). Changes an agent makes through the symlink affect the folder in the original checkout.
+
+Worktree sessions use **Allow all** and don't offer manual approval prompts. Folder sessions offer the [permission levels](/docs/agents/run/approvals.md#permission-levels) supported by the selected harness. For operating system-level file system and network restrictions, configure [agent sandboxing](/docs/agents/run/agent-sandboxing.md).
+
+Dev Container sessions work directly in the container workspace and don't support **New Worktree**. See [Run a session in a Dev Container](#run-a-session-in-a-dev-container).
+
+## Work with multiple sessions
+
+Use separate sessions for independent tasks, such as updating documentation in one project while investigating a bug in another. Separate conversations don't isolate files: sessions using the same folder can edit the same files. For parallel implementation in one repository, review the [worktree and permission requirements](#choose-where-an-agent-makes-changes) and follow [Delegate two tasks without mixing their changes](/docs/agents/guides/delegate-two-tasks.md).
+
+The sessions list shows sessions across all your workspaces. You can group sessions by workspace or time, create custom groups with distinct icons and colors, pin sessions, and rearrange items with drag and drop. Learn how to [organize and manage sessions](/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions.md#sessions-list).
+
+### Arrange sessions in a grid
+
+Arrange parallel sessions in a two-dimensional grid to monitor progress and compare results. To open another session in the grid:
+
+* To keep the active session visible while you start a new session, hold ``Alt`` (``Option`` on macOS) and select **New**.
+* Right-click a session in the sessions list and select **Open to the Side**.
+* Drag a session from the sessions list into the view area.
+* Hold ``Alt`` and select a session in the sessions list.
+
+Drag a session to the top, bottom, left, or right edge of another session to create a horizontal or vertical split. A placement preview shows where the session appears.
+
+<video src="../images/agents-window/sessions-grid.mp4" title="Video showing agent sessions arranged in a grid in the Agents window." autoplay loop controls muted></video>
+
+Only one session pane is active at a time. Select a pane to make it active and direct the **Files**, **Changes**, **Terminal**, **Tasks**, and browser actions to that session. Selecting another session in the list replaces an unpinned active view.
+
+Open the **Session Layout** submenu from a session header or its overflow menu. From there, you can select **Arrange Sessions in a Balanced Grid**, focus a session in a direction, move the active session, or increase or decrease its width or height. The default directional focus shortcuts are ``Shortcut: sessions.focusSessionLeft``, ``Shortcut: sessions.focusSessionRight``, ``Shortcut: sessions.focusSessionAbove``, and ``Shortcut: sessions.focusSessionBelow``.
```

 # Use memory with agents in VS Code
 
-Agents in Visual Studio Code use memory to retain context across conversations. Rather than starting from scratch each session, agents recall your preferences, apply lessons from previous tasks, and build up knowledge about your codebase over time.
+Memory helps agents reuse coding preferences and repository knowledge without asking you to repeat them in every conversation. The memory system depends on your [agent harness](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md):
+
+* **Copilot harness**: Use [[copilot.copilot_memory]](#copilot-memory) to store repository facts and user preferences in the cloud.
+
+* **Local harness**: Use [memory files](#local-memory-files) for persistent notes and temporary session context.
 
 For background on how memory fits into the agent architecture, see [Agents concepts](/docs/agents/concepts/agents.md#memory).
 
-This article explains how to use the memory tool in VS Code and manage memory files.
+This article shows how to set up cloud-backed memory, review or delete stored information, and manage local memory files.

 Launch a chat prompt that asks the agent to remember a coding preference.

 </div>
 
-## Memory tool
+## [copilot.copilot_memory]
 
-The memory tool is a built-in agent tool that allows agents to save and recall notes as they work. You can also explicitly ask the agent to remember something. User, repository, and session memory are stored locally on your machine.
+Sessions that use the Copilot harness locally can use [copilot.copilot_memory], the same cloud memory service used by Copilot CLI, Copilot cloud agent, and code review. Memories captured by one supported feature can inform another, although supported scopes vary. For example, code review uses repository facts, not user preferences.
+
+### Set up cloud-backed memory
+
+[copilot.copilot_memory] is on by default in VS Code. To use it:
+
+1. [Sign in to GitHub Copilot](/docs/setup/copilot.md) with your [product.prodname_github] account.
+
+1. In your [personal Copilot settings on [product.prodname_github]](https://github.com/settings/copilot/features), check that **[copilot.copilot_memory]** is **Enabled**. If your plan is managed by an organization or enterprise, its policies must permit memory.
+
+1. Check that ``chat.copilot.memory.enabled`` is on in VS Code Settings. If you previously turned it off, it stays off until you turn it on.
+
+1. Create or resume a local Copilot session in the Chat view or Agents window. The setting applies to sessions created or resumed after it changes.
+
+The VS Code editor preview-features policy doesn't control cloud memory.
+
+Repository memories require a [product.prodname_github]-hosted repository. User preferences are tied to your signed-in [product.prodname_github] account and can apply across repositories.
+
+If the setting is on but memory isn't available, check your [product.prodname_github] account settings and organization policies. Contact your administrator if a required feature is unavailable or locked. For account eligibility and default billing-entity requirements when you have multiple licenses, see [Managing [copilot.copilot_memory] for your personal account](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/copilot-memory/manage-for-yourself).
+
+### Choose what to remember
+
+Cloud-backed memory has two scopes:
+
+| Scope | What it stores | Where it applies |
+|---|---|---|
+| **Repository** | Durable codebase facts and conventions, supported by citations to the code. | Shared with people who have access to the repository and [copilot.copilot_memory]. Used only for that repository. |
+| **User** | Coding and workflow preferences that apply across repositories. | Used in your own supported Copilot interactions, not other contributors' interactions. |
+
+Storing repository facts requires write access to the repository and memory enabled for your account. On organization- or enterprise-managed plans, administrators can also review and delete user preferences. See [Managing [copilot.copilot_memory] for an organization or enterprise](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/copilot-memory/manage-as-administrator).
+
+> [!CAUTION]
+> Don't store credentials, secrets, or sensitive personal information in memory. Repository facts are shared, not private notes. Keep reviewed team requirements in source-controlled project documentation or [custom instructions](/docs/agent-customization/custom-instructions.md).
+
+### Store, recall, and correct memories
+
+Ask the agent to remember a durable convention or preference. State the scope when it matters:
+
+```prompt
+Find how this repository verifies changes, and remember the command for this repository.
+```
+
+```prompt
+Across all my repositories, remember that I prefer concise commit message subjects.
+```
+
+The agent recalls relevant repository facts and user preferences when a session starts. It uses **Store Memory** to save new information. When it verifies an existing memory, it can upvote it instead of storing a duplicate. It can downvote an outdated memory and store a corrected replacement.
+
+If a remembered convention is wrong, point the agent to the current code and ask it to correct the memory. Use persistent memory for durable information, not temporary task status.
+
+### Review and delete cloud memories
+
+Review stored information on [product.prodname_github]:
+
+* **User preferences**: Open your [personal memory settings](https://github.com/settings/copilot/memory) to view and delete preferences.
+* **Repository facts**: With repository administration access, open the repository's **Settings** > **Copilot** > **Memory**. Deleting a repository fact removes it for everyone who uses memory in that repository.
+
+Asking the agent to forget a cloud memory downvotes it rather than permanently deleting it. To permanently delete it, use the [product.prodname_github] settings above. The local memory-file commands below don't delete cloud memories.
+
+Facts and preferences that go unused are automatically deleted after 28 days. Successful validation and use can reset that timer. Learn more about [memory retention and validation](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/prompting-and-context/copilot-memory#retention-and-validation).
+
+To stop using cloud memory in newly created or resumed VS Code sessions, turn off ``chat.copilot.memory.enabled``. Your personal memory setting on [product.prodname_github] controls its use across supported Copilot features. To remove stored information, delete it on [product.prodname_github].
+
+## Local memory files
+
+The Local harness has a separate file-based memory tool that saves and recalls notes as the agent works. You can also explicitly ask the agent to remember something. By default, user, repository, and session memory are stored locally on your machine.
+
+The following sections describe local memory files. If repository memory is backed by [product.prodname_github] instead, manage those repository facts on [product.prodname_github], not with the local file-management commands.
 
 ### Memory scopes

```diff
+**MetaDescription**: Find, continue, organize, and finish agent sessions in VS Code without losing track of ongoing work.
 
 # Manage agent sessions in VS Code
 
-A [session](/docs/agents/concepts/sessions.md) is the unit of work with an agent in Visual Studio Code. It brings together the workspace, code changes, and one or more chats for a task. Each chat has its own conversation history and context. This article describes how to manage these conversations and organize sessions across the [Chat view](/docs/agents/run/chat-view.md) and the [Agents window](/docs/agents/run/agents-window.md).
-
-<div class="docs-action" data-show-in-doc="false" data-show-in-sidebar="true" title="Get started with agents">
-Follow a hands-on tutorial to build an app with AI agents in VS Code.
-
-* [Start agentic coding tutorial](/docs/agents/agents-tutorial.md)
-
-</div>
-
-## Start an agent session
+Use the sessions list to return to an agent task, monitor ongoing work, and put completed work away. This article shows how to manage sessions in the [Chat view](/docs/agents/run/chat-view.md) and the [Agents window](/docs/agents/run/agents-window.md).
+
+A [session](/docs/agents/concepts/sessions.md) groups the workspace, code changes, and conversations for a task. Each conversation has its own history and context. If you're starting your first task, follow the [agents quickstart](/docs/agents/quickstart.md).
+
+## Find and resume a session
+
+Open an existing session to continue its conversation rather than start the task again.
+
+1. Open the sessions list in the interface you use:
+
+    | Interface | Location and scope |
+    |---|---|
+    | Chat view | The list is at the top of the view and shows sessions for the current workspace, grouped by time. With no workspace open, it shows sessions across workspaces. |
+    | Agents window | The list is in the left sidebar and shows sessions across workspaces. Sessions are grouped by workspace by default. |
+
+1. Select the session to open its conversation.
+
+1. If your session is completed, it may not appear in the active sessions list. Change the list filter from active sessions to **Archived** (Chat view) or **Done** (Agents window).
+
+1. Review the previous messages and changes before sending a follow-up. For an archived session, [restore it first](#archive-sessions).
+
+If the list isn't visible in the Chat view, right-click in an empty chat and select **Show Sessions**. For display options, see [sessions list layout](/docs/agents/run/chat-view.md#sessions-list-layout).
+
+### Find a missing session
+
+Check these items before creating a replacement session:
+
+* **Workspace and host**: Open the original workspace or connect to the host where the session runs. The Agents window lets you browse across workspaces.
+* **State filters**: Include **Archived** or **Done** sessions, not only active sessions.
+* **Other applications**: Check the [External filter and discovery limits](#view-sessions-from-other-applications).
+* **Supported interface**: Local harness sessions and sessions from the [product.prodname_openai_codex] extension are editor-only. Check [which sessions support both interfaces](/docs/agents/concepts/sessions.md#sessions-across-surfaces).
+
+To find earlier work by topic, file, or pull request instead of browsing the list, [query session history](/docs/agents/run/sessions/session-history.md#query-session-history-with-chronicle). Synced history doesn't by itself provide access to a running agent.
+
+### Continue between the Chat view and Agents window
+
+Supported Copilot and [product.prodname_anthropic_claude_short] sessions are available in both interfaces. [product.prodname_openai_codex_short] requires the [experimental Agent Host integration](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#codex). Switching interfaces doesn't change the session's harness, workspace, or worktree.
+
+For a Copilot session with a project:
+
+* **From the Agents window**: Select **Open in Editor** in the title bar. The editor opens the project with the session available in the Chat view.
+* **From the Chat view**: Select **Open in Agents** in the application title bar, then select the existing session from the sessions list.
+
+To change the harness instead, see [Continue with a different harness](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#continue-with-a-different-harness).
 
 > [!NOTE]
-> Claude and Codex harnesses are disabled when [Copilot enterprise-managed settings apply](/docs/enterprise/manage-ai-settings.md#claude-and-codex-availability). Existing sessions are not deleted by this restriction. Contact the IT team that deployed the settings to discuss access.
-
-Start a new session when you begin an independent task or need a different workspace or configuration. For a fresh conversation that shares an existing session's workspace and code changes, [start another chat in that session](#run-multiple-chats-in-a-session), where supported.
-
-Choose the surface that matches your workflow:
-
-* Use the [Chat view](/docs/agents/run/chat-view.md#start-a-session) for a workspace-scoped, code-first session beside the editor.
-* Use the [Agents window](/docs/agents/run/agents-window.md#start-an-agent-session) to start and monitor sessions across workspaces, attach related projects or GitHub items, or start from an existing pull request. On Windows, you can also launch the Agents window directly by right-clicking the VS Code application icon in the taskbar and selecting **Agents Window**.
-
-You can continue supported sessions between these surfaces after starting work. Availability depends on the harness; see [Sessions across surfaces](/docs/agents/concepts/sessions.md#sessions-across-surfaces). To choose an interface and follow the workflow, see [Run agents](/docs/agents/run/overview.md). To send and steer requests after a session starts, see [Use chat in VS Code](/docs/chat/chat-overview.md).
+> [product.prodname_anthropic_claude_short] and [product.prodname_openai_codex_short] harnesses are disabled when [Copilot enterprise-managed settings apply](/docs/enterprise/manage-ai-settings.md#claude-and-codex-availability). Existing sessions aren't deleted. Contact the IT team that deployed the settings to discuss access.
+
+### View sessions from other applications
+
+You can open supported local sessions from Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, Claude Code, and [product.prodname_openai_codex_short] in either interface.
+
+Open the sessions list filter and select **External** to choose which discovered sessions appear:
+
+| Filter | Sessions shown |
+|---|---|
+| **None** | No external sessions. |
+| **Recent** | Up to two most recently updated external sessions from the last seven days. At startup, sessions older than the second-most-recently updated local session are hidden. |
+| **Last 24 Hours** | Sessions updated within the last 24 hours. |
+| **Last 7 Days** (default) | Sessions updated within the last seven days. |
+| **Last 30 Days** | Sessions updated within the last 30 days. |
+
+The filter applies to both interfaces and is also configurable with ``chat.agentSessions.showExternal`` (Experimental). Discovery has separate limits: Copilot only considers supported local sessions updated within the last seven days, even if you select **Last 30 Days**.
+
+When you open an external session in the Agents window, a one-time banner identifies its origin and lets you choose which external sessions to show. If that choice hides the open session, you're asked to confirm it. After you send a message from VS Code, the session is no longer external and the **External** filter no longer controls its visibility.
+
+For an external [product.prodname_openai_codex_short] session, only one application can write to the chat at a time. If **This chat is open in another app** appears, fully quit the other application and select **Retry**. The transcript, draft, and attachments remain available while sending, queueing, and resending are blocked. Retry doesn't send the draft. Send it yourself after the banner disappears.
+
+### Use Copilot CLI from the terminal
+
+If the session's context menu includes **Resume in Terminal**, select it to continue in GitHub Copilot CLI. Not every harness or session type provides this action. Otherwise, continue in a supported VS Code interface.
+
+To begin a separate terminal conversation, [start a new CLI session](/docs/agents/run/chat-view.md#start-a-copilot-cli-session). Starting a new CLI session doesn't resume an existing conversation.
+
+### Continue on another device or in the cloud
+
+| Where the session runs | How to continue |
+|---|---|
+| A remote host | Use [GitHub Environments (Preview), SSH, or dev tunnels](/docs/agents/run/remote-agent-sessions.md#choose-how-to-connect), then open the existing session. The host must remain running and reachable. |
+| A managed cloud environment `feature(cloud-sessions)` | [Reconnect to the existing cloud session](/docs/agents/run/cloud-sandbox-sessions.md#continue-an-existing-cloud-session). Execution stays in the managed environment. |
+
+To move from local work to cloud execution, [start a separate cloud session](/docs/agents/run/cloud-sandbox-sessions.md#start-a-cloud-session).
+
+For a hands-on walkthrough, [start a task in a cloud session and continue it from a regular terminal with Copilot CLI](/docs/agents/cloud-continuity-tutorial.md) `feature(cloud-sessions)`.
+
+## Start a new or related conversation
+
+Choose a conversation based on whether you need the discussion so far:
+
+| Your goal | Action |
+|---|---|
+| Continue the same task | [Resume the existing conversation](#find-and-resume-a-session). |
```

```diff
 # Review and revert agent changes
 
-When you work with an agent in Visual Studio Code, it can change multiple files in your project. This article explains how to inspect, revise, integrate, or discard these AI-generated changes.
-
-The available review controls depend primarily on the agent harness:
-
-| Session | How changes are tracked | Review workflow |
-|---------|-------------------------|-----------------|
-| Copilot, Claude, and Codex harness sessions | Edits are saved directly in the session's folder or isolated Git worktree. They don't wait in a pending review state. | Inspect diffs in the Chat view, Agents window, or Source Control. Use checkpoints or Git to revert unwanted changes. |
-| Local harness sessions and existing extension-host sessions | Edits are saved directly. Supported edits are also marked as pending. | Inspect each pending edit in the editor. Use **Keep** to acknowledge it or **Undo** to revert it. |
-| Cloud sessions | Changes are committed to a branch and returned through a pull request. | Review the pull request on GitHub or check out the branch locally. |

-> [!NOTE]
-> Claude and Codex harnesses are disabled when [Copilot enterprise-managed settings apply](/docs/enterprise/manage-ai-settings.md#claude-and-codex-availability). Contact the IT team that deployed the settings to discuss access.
+Use this guide to review agent changes, request revisions, and undo unwanted edits in a folder, worktree, or cloud session.

+## Review pending edits with the working set
+
+When you use Copilot and Local harness sessions in the editor window, supported file edits are tracked as pending review (working set). **Keep** retains the changes and clears their pending-review state. **Undo** reverts them without rewinding the agent conversation.
+
+Pending edits are already saved to disk, so running your application or tests uses the changed files. You don't need Git to review them, and **Keep** doesn't stage or commit them.
+
+To review pending edits:
+
+1. Open a file from the changed-files list in the Chat view.
+
+1. Review the highlighted changes in the editor. Use the ``Up`` and ``Down`` controls in the editor overlay to navigate between edits.
+
+1. Select **Keep** or **Undo** beside an individual change, or use the file-level or all-files review controls to resolve multiple pending edits at once.
+
+Staging changes in the Source Control view automatically keeps the corresponding pending edits.
+
+> [!NOTE]
+> The working set only tracks changes from supported agent edit tools. Changes made through terminal commands, scripts, or other untracked tools don't appear. Review these changes separately, and use Source Control to inspect changed and untracked files when the folder uses Git.
+
+### Configure review controls
+
+* ``chat.editor.workingSet.enabled`` `feature(editor-working-set)` (Copilot only): Show the working set. Defaults to `true`.
+
+* ``chat.editing.revealNextChangeOnResolve``: Set to `false` to stay at the current change after keeping or undoing an edit, instead of navigating to the next pending change.
+

+For Claude or Codex harness sessions in the editor window, the Agents window, and cloud sessions, compare diffs instead of keeping or undoing pending edits.

+
+Use any of these review options:
+
+* Select the changed-files pill to open a multi-diff editor with all changes.
+
+* Select a changed file in the agent's response to open its diff.
+
+* In the editor, use the [Source Control view](/docs/sourcecontrol/staging-commits.md) to review changed and untracked files when the folder uses Git.
+
+### Review changes in the Agents window
+
+1. Open the **Changes** view in the side panel by using the layout controls in the title bar, or use the ``Shortcut: workbench.action.toggleAuxiliaryBar`` keyboard shortcut.
 
 1. Select a file in the **Changes** view to open a diff of the agent's edits.
 
-    The **Changes** view groups edits outside the workspace under **Other Files**. These files, such as plans in the session-state folder, aren't committed with workspace changes. Files changed only through terminal commands or scripts might not appear in tool-specific change tracking. Review the session's folder or worktree in Source Control as well, including untracked files.
+    **Other Files** groups edits outside the workspace, such as session plans, which aren't committed with workspace changes. Also check Source Control for untracked files and changes made outside tracked edit tools.
 
     > [!TIP]
     > Use the **Branch Changes** dropdown to choose which changeset to review.
 
-1. To provide feedback, select a range of code in a changed file, and enter feedback in the inline comment box that appears.
-
-1. Continue reviewing and providing feedback on other changes as needed. Select **Submit Feedback** to send them to the agent.

-    The agent reads your comments, makes the requested edits, and resolves each comment. Resolved comments disappear from the diff view.
```

```diff
 # Run and manage remote agent sessions
 
-The [Agents window](/docs/agents/run/agents-window.md) lets you connect to remote machines to start agent sessions or check in on existing ones. You can connect over SSH, through a dev tunnel, or use the Agents window directly in a browser from any device.
-
-This is useful when you want to take advantage of a remote machine's resources, work from a mobile device, or check in on your agent's progress when you're away from your main development machine.
-

-
-## Start a chat without a workspace on a remote host
-
-Use a chat without a workspace when a task needs the resources or environment of a remote host but doesn't need a repository. First, enable ``sessions.chat.unifiedWorkspacePicker.enabled`` and connect the host over SSH or a dev tunnel.
-
-To start a chat without a workspace:
-
-1. Select **New** or press ``Shortcut: workbench.action.chat.newChat`` to start a new agent session.
-
-1. In the workspace picker, select the **Chat** entry for a connected remote host without choosing a folder. The entry identifies the host where the chat runs.
-
-1. Choose an agent harness, enter your prompt, and press ``Enter``.
```
