-The main workspace picker also shows folders from connected remote hosts alongside local folders. Select a remote folder there when the task needs an existing workspace.
+Continue agent work from another app or device while your workspace, tools, and running sessions stay on your development machine. Use GitHub Environments to make that machine available across supported Copilot clients, or use SSH and dev tunnels to connect from VS Code.
+
+This guide helps you choose a connection, share a host, manage remote environments, and continue an existing remote session without starting over.
+
+To prevent this client from connecting to remote agent hosts, turn off ``chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled``.
+
+## Choose how to connect
+
+Choose based on where you want to interact with the session and how you can reach its host:
+
+| Connection | When to use it |
+|------------|----------------|
+| **[GitHub Environments (Preview)](#github-environments-preview)** | Register your machine for remote agent access from supported Copilot clients, including VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, Copilot CLI, GitHub.com, and GitHub Mobile. Available session types and actions vary by client. |
+| **[SSH](#connect-via-ssh)** | Connect the Agents window to a remote host through SSH. |
+| **[Dev tunnels](#connect-via-dev-tunnel)** | Connect from VS Code or the [browser-based Agents window](#use-the-agents-window-in-the-browser) to a host through an authenticated tunnel. |
+
+SSH and dev tunnels provide VS Code-specific client-to-host access in these workflows. GitHub Environments provides machine registration for access across supported Copilot surfaces, not just another VS Code instance.
+
+The files and development tools stay on the machine where the agent runs. Keep that machine powered on and reachable, and keep its agent host running. For a session hosted by desktop VS Code, keep the application running.
+
+Connecting doesn't move a local session or copy its workspace to another machine. To continue an existing remote session, connect to the host where it already runs. For managed compute that doesn't depend on keeping your own host online, use [cloud sessions](/docs/agents/run/cloud-sandbox-sessions.md) `feature(cloud-sessions)`.
+
+## Manage remote environments (Experimental)
+
+Use the Remote Environments editor in the Agents window to find and manage your remote machines in one place. The table groups known SSH hosts, dev tunnels, and WSL distributions on Windows. When [GitHub Environments](#github-environments-preview) is available and enabled, the **Environments** group also lists your registered machines, including offline ones. These are user-shared machines, not the managed environments used by cloud sessions.
+
+Remote environment management requires ``sessions.chat.experimental.environmentPicker``, ``sessions.chat.experimental.environmentPickerManageRemotes``, and ``chat.remoteAgentHostsEnabled``. All three settings are on by default.
+
+![Screen showing the Remote Environments editor in the Agents window.](../images/remote-agent-sessions/remote-environments-editor.png)
+
+### Open remote environment management
+
+Run **Agents: Manage Remote Environments** from the Command Palette (``Shortcut: workbench.action.showCommands``), or select **Manage Remote Environments** from the sessions list **More Actions** (`...`) menu.
+
+If the experimental new-session composer layout is enabled (``sessions.chat.experimental.newSessionComposerLayout``), you can also open the editor from the **Environment** picker:
+
+1. Create a new chat or session in the Agents window.
+
+1. Open the **Environment** picker and select **Manage**.
+
+    ![Screen showing the Environment picker and its Manage entry.](../images/remote-agent-sessions/environment-picker-manage.png)
+
+### Find and organize remote machines
+
+Use the table to search, connect, and organize your remote machines. Keep these behaviors in mind:
+
+* Disconnecting doesn't stop running tasks. Refreshing discovers machines without connecting.
+
+* Renaming or hiding a machine affects only this client. Hiding doesn't disconnect it or remove sessions. Leave a name empty to restore the default.
+
+* **Delete** is available only for GitHub Environments. It removes the registration and disconnects this client without deleting files. The environment can reappear if its owning application registers it again.
+
+## GitHub Environments (Preview)
+
+GitHub Environments supports continuity across apps and devices: register your development machine with your [product.prodname_github] account, then access its supported agent sessions from another client. Registration doesn't provision a new machine or copy your code.
+
+**Prerequisites**:
+
+* Sign in to the host and connecting client with the same [product.prodname_github] account.
+
+* Check your [organization's controls](/docs/enterprise/manage-ai-settings.md#control-github-environments-preview) if the option is managed or unavailable.
+
+### Register your machine
+
+On the machine that contains your workspace and runs the agent:
+
+1. Open **Remote Connections** in the Agents window title bar or the editor's Chat view input area.
+
+1. Select **GitHub Environments**. Selecting this method starts sharing the machine. Complete any sign-in or confirmation prompts.
+
+1. Check the registered environment name in the menu. Select the name if you want to rename the environment so you can recognize it on another device.
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> Connected clients receive trusted-owner access to the host's sessions, tools, and workspace resources. Session actions are mirrored to [product.prodname_github] for catalog and history storage, and conversation content is not end-to-end encrypted. Review [remote connection security](/docs/agents/run/security.md#remote-connections-and-github-environments) before sharing a machine.
+
+The ``chat.agentHost.remoteConnections`` setting records your preferred connection method. Changing the setting directly turns sharing off. To start sharing, select the method in **Remote Connections**.
+
+### Connect from another client
+
+In another desktop VS Code instance:
+
+1. Sign in with the same [product.prodname_github] account you used to register the host.
+
+1. Open the Command Palette (``Shortcut: workbench.action.showCommands``) and run **Connect to Environment...**.
+
+1. Select the registered machine. Use **Refresh Environments** in the picker if it hasn't appeared yet.
+
+1. After connecting, [select the existing remote session](#continue-an-existing-remote-session).
+
+For other supported Copilot clients, use that client's environment connection controls. Registration makes the machine discoverable; it doesn't guarantee that every client supports the same harnesses, sessions, or actions.
+
+On desktop VS Code, discovering a machine doesn't connect to it for the first time. Connect explicitly. With ``chat.remoteAgentHostsAutoConnect`` on, previously connected online environments can reconnect for the same profile and account. Explicitly disconnecting suppresses automatic reconnection until you connect manually again.
+
```

@@ -33,6 +33,32 @@
 ## Trust boundaries
 
 VS Code's security model uses trust boundaries to limit the potential impact of untrusted code. Trust decisions cover the workspace, extension publishers, MCP servers, and network domains, and you can revoke trust at any time. Related boundaries can share a decision. For example, MCP servers in `.vscode/mcp.json` and workspace-root `.mcp.json` inherit Workspace Trust. For a description of each boundary, see [trust boundaries](/docs/agents/concepts/trust-and-safety.md#trust-boundaries).
+
+## Remote connections and GitHub Environments
+
+[GitHub Environments (Preview)](/docs/agents/run/remote-agent-sessions.md#github-environments-preview) lets you register a development machine for access from supported Copilot clients. Connected clients receive trusted-owner access to sessions, tools, and workspace resources on that machine. Only connect from clients and devices you trust, and protect the [product.prodname_github] account used to register the host.
+
+Session actions are mirrored to [product.prodname_github] for catalog and history storage. Conversation content is not end-to-end encrypted. Review the sharing disclosure before registering a host and check your organization's data-handling requirements.
+
+For VS Code-specific connections over SSH or dev tunnels, protect the SSH credentials or tunnel account. Require authentication for tunnels; don't expose an agent host through anonymous access.
+
+Disconnecting a client doesn't stop the host's tasks. To stop sharing from the host, select **Remote Connections** > **Off**. To halt active work, stop the task in its session. Neither action undoes completed file edits, commands, or external effects. See [disconnect or stop sharing](/docs/agents/run/remote-agent-sessions.md#disconnect-or-stop-sharing).
+
+## Cloud sessions
+
+[Cloud sessions](/docs/agents/run/cloud-sandbox-sessions.md) `feature(cloud-sessions)` run agent tools in a managed environment, not in your local workspace. Check the repository, cloud session's permissions, and data-handling requirements before sending code or task context. Local editor state, extension tools, and uncommitted files aren't automatically transferred.
+
+Managed compute is a different boundary from [process-level agent sandboxing](/docs/agents/run/agent-sandboxing.md). Don't assume that local sandbox or approval settings configure the cloud service. Use the controls available in the cloud session and review its changes and test results before integration.
+
+Closing a client or marking a task as done isn't a cloud-resource shutdown action. Stopping a request doesn't undo completed actions, and deleting a task shouldn't be treated as confirmation that its compute environment was deleted. See [cloud session lifecycle guidance](/docs/agents/run/cloud-sandbox-sessions.md#review-work-and-finish-a-session).
+
+## Unattended cloud automations
+
+[Cloud automations](/docs/agents/run/automations.md#create-an-automation) `feature(cloud-automations)` run saved tasks on GitHub when a schedule or supported repository event triggers them. Restrict their allowed tools, test the prompt with a manual run, and use event filters and **Require write access to trigger** to limit which events can start work. Local approval and sandbox settings don't configure the cloud service.
+
+Keep secrets out of automation prompts. An **Only me** automation definition is private, but its run sessions and logs can be visible to people with repository access. Review [cloud automation security and usage](/docs/agents/run/automations.md#cloud-automation-security-and-usage) before enabling unattended work.
+
+Closing the application or turning off cloud controls doesn't disable GitHub triggers. Disable the automation to prevent future runs, and use **Stop** separately to request cancellation of an active run. Neither action reverses completed changes.
 
 ## How VS Code protects your environment
 
@@ -63,7 +89,7 @@
 
 VS Code uses a permission-based security model where you maintain control over potentially risky operations.
 
-* **Permission levels**: In a Copilot harness session, use the [permissions picker](/docs/agents/run/approvals.md#permission-levels) to choose how tool calls are approved. **Manual permissions** uses your configured approval settings. **Assisted permissions** `feature(assisted-permissions)` uses an LLM judge to evaluate each tool call and asks for your approval when the judge does not approve it. **Allow all** auto-approves all tool calls. **Autopilot** is an agent mode that auto-approves all tools and drives the agent to continue working until the task is complete. Available controls depend on the harness and code isolation. For Local harness sessions, Autopilot is a permission level instead.
+* **Permission levels**: In a Copilot harness session, use the [permissions picker](/docs/agents/run/approvals.md#permission-levels) to choose how tool calls are approved. **Manual permissions** uses your configured approval settings. **Assisted permissions** uses an LLM judge to evaluate each tool call and asks for your approval when the judge does not approve it. **Allow all** auto-approves all tool calls. **Autopilot** is an agent mode that auto-approves all tools and drives the agent to continue working until the task is complete. Available controls depend on the harness and code isolation. For Local harness sessions, Autopilot is a permission level instead.
 
 * **Terminal approval**: Before executing terminal commands, the agent requests explicit user approval. When terminal auto-approval is enabled, configurable per-command rules (including regex patterns) auto-approve safe commands while prompting for potentially dangerous ones. All subcommands in a compound command must match an approved rule.
 
@@ -71,7 +97,7 @@
 
 * **URL and domain approval**: When the agent fetches content from a URL, VS Code uses a two-step approval flow. First, it asks you to trust the domain (integrated with the Trusted Domains list). Then, after the content is fetched, it presents the content for review before it is passed to the model.

+## Generate and edit images (Experimental)
+
+Generate illustrations, UI mockups, or other image assets directly in chat. In a [Copilot harness](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md) session, the agent uses a dedicated image-generation model, separate from the language model selected for the conversation.
+
+1. Verify that ``chat.copilot.imageGeneration.model`` is set to an image-generation model.
+
+1. Ask the agent to generate an image. Describe the subject, style, and intended use. For example:
+
+    ```prompt
+    Generate a wide mountain landscape illustration for my app's welcome screen. Use muted colors and leave space for a heading on the left.
+    ```
+
+1. Review the result and send a follow-up request to edit it:
+
+    ```prompt
+    Make it nighttime and add a few stars, keeping the space for the heading.
+    ```
+
+1. Select **Save** next to the image in chat to download it to your device.
+
+To edit an existing image, [attach the image as context](/docs/chat/copilot-chat-context.md#vision) and describe the changes. You can also ask for multiple images, such as three variations of an illustration with different color palettes.
+
+Image generation requires access to the image model and follows [tool permission controls](/docs/agents/run/approvals.md). Prompts and selected reference images are sent to the image model. Generation and editing use [AI credits](/docs/agents/concepts/language-models.md#ai-credits-and-model-costs) in addition to those used by the conversation model. Check the model setting for current rates, and expand an image-generation tool call to review its AI-credit usage, duration, and input and output usage.
+
+To request a visible 'Made with AI' label on generated or edited images, turn on ``chat.copilot.imageGeneration.watermark``. This setting defaults to `false` and applies to new and existing Copilot sessions without turning image generation on. The image model generates the label, so it isn't guaranteed. Turning the setting off doesn't remove existing labels from reference images.
+
+To turn off image generation, set ``chat.copilot.imageGeneration.model`` to **Off**. This prevents future image-generation tool calls, but doesn't prevent the agent from creating SVGs or other graphics by writing code.

 ## Common built-in tool workflows
 
+### Coordinate work across sessions
+
+In sessions using the Copilot or [product.prodname_anthropic_claude_short] harness, agents can use built-in session-management tools to coordinate related work. These tools are also available with the [experimental [product.prodname_openai_codex_short] integration](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#codex).
+
+An agent can:
+
+* List sessions and inspect their status, workspace, and file changes.
+* Create sessions or nested sessions.
+* Read another conversation's recent context.
+* Send messages to start or steer follow-up work.
+
+State both the relationship between tasks and where the new work should run:
+
+* **Related work**: Request a nested session that reuses the current workspace and checkout for research or planning that can share files.
+* **Independent work**: Request a separate session. Omit the workspace for work that doesn't need repository files, or choose a trusted folder. Request a new worktree when code changes must be isolated.
+
+For related, read-only work:
+
+```prompt
+Create a nested session under this session that reuses the current workspace and checkout to review the authentication flow. Do not modify files.
+```
+
+For unrelated work without repository files:
+
+```prompt
+Create an independent session with no workspace to research licensing options for a separate project.
+```
+
+For isolated implementation in a known project:
+
+```prompt
+Create an independent session in the vscode workspace with a new worktree to implement and test the authentication change.
+```
+
+The tools use `currentSession` for nested work and `independent` for separate sessions. A project name can identify the workspace instead of an absolute path or URI. If names are ambiguous, the agent reports matching projects rather than choosing one. Remote workspace URIs and multi-root project working directories are also supported.
+
+When a tool creates or targets a session, an **Open Session** pill lets you jump to it. To monitor and finish the work yourself, see [Manage agent sessions](/docs/agents/run/sessions/manage-sessions.md).
+
+Keep these constraints in mind:
+
+* Sending a message to another session always requires confirmation.
+* Agents can't send messages to the chat they are currently running in.
+* Creation and messaging limits guard against unbounded fan-out.
+* Archived sessions are excluded from listings unless explicitly requested.
+
+The experimental ``chat.agentHost.agentOrchestrationLimits`` setting defaults to `on`. It limits how many sessions and chats each source session creates and how many messages it sends within a sliding one-hour window, as well as recursive session creation depth. A busy session doesn't consume another session's allowance, and capacity returns as earlier actions leave the window.
+
+Setting it to `off` removes these limits without changing confirmation requirements or input validation. Changes apply without restarting the Agent Host. Reaching a limit doesn't interrupt work already running.
+
 ### Use browser tools
 
 Browser tools give agents an interactive way to validate web applications. Instead of inspecting only the source code, an agent can run your app, open it in the integrated browser, exercise a user flow, inspect page content and console errors, and fix problems it discovers.
@@ -192,6 +241,69 @@
 With [Python Environments](/docs/python/environments.md#terminal-settings) installed and ``python-envs.terminal.autoActivationType`` set to `shellStartup`, the selected workspace environment is also activated.
 
 This setting does not apply to remote sessions or the custom terminal tool override.
+
+## Control desktop applications (Experimental)
+
+Use Computer Use when a task needs a desktop application that the agent's other tools can't reach. [product.prodname_github]'s Computer Use plugin lets the agent see application windows, click, type, and scroll. For web applications, use [browser tools](#use-browser-tools) instead.
+
+Computer Use is available for local [Copilot harness sessions](/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses.md#copilot) on macOS and Windows. It isn't available for the Local, Claude, or Codex harnesses, Linux, or remote or cloud hosts.
+
+> [!CAUTION]
+> Computer Use can read and change content in applications outside your workspace. Approve access only to apps needed for your task, and avoid exposing sensitive content in application windows. See [desktop application access risks](/docs/agents/run/security.md#security-risks-to-be-aware-of).
+
+### Turn on Computer Use
+
+Computer Use is Experimental and off by default. To use it:
+
+1. Turn on ``chat.agentHost.computerUse.enabled`` in Settings, and restart VS Code.
+
+1. Start a new local Copilot chat in the Chat view or Agents window. The plugin downloads automatically on first use.
+
+1. Ask the agent to perform a task in a desktop application. For example:
+
+    ```prompt
+    Open Calculator and use it to compute 12 times 7.
+    ```
+
+1. When the agent asks **Turn on Computer Use?**, review its reason and select **Turn On**.
+
+1. On macOS, [grant the required system permissions](#grant-macos-permissions). On both platforms, approve access to each application when requested.
+
+You can also run `/computer on` in a Copilot chat. If you select **Not Now**, the agent continues without Computer Use and doesn't ask again in that chat. Run `/computer on` if you change your mind.
```

### [MODIFICADO] `microsoft_vscode-docs::release-notes/v1_144.md`
- **URL Canónica**: https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_144

- **Hash Nuevo**: `bc09923fe097ce1745ab20ff60974a15abdeb1e114eac0608ed25f9010c9fd93`

```diff
--- microsoft_vscode-docs::release-notes/v1_144.md (prev: 82c1dfcc)
+++ microsoft_vscode-docs::release-notes/v1_144.md (new: bc09923f)
@@ -1,46 +1,565 @@
-**MetaDescription**: Learn what is new in Visual Studio Code 1.144 (Insiders)
+**MetaDescription**: Learn what's new in Visual Studio Code 1.144
 
 # Visual Studio Code 1.144
 
-Follow us on [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/showcase/vs-code), [X](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=533687), [Bluesky](https://bsky.app/profile/vscode.dev), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/vscode)
+## Release recap
+
+The road to GitHub Universe ([join us virtually!](https://githubuniverse.com/)) is paved with lots of pull requests! So, let's take a step back and look at what we've shipped recently.
+
+* Remember when agent sessions would stop as soon as you closed your client? We built the [Agent Host](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/concepts/agent-host), a separate process that keeps your agents running, on your local machine or remotely.
+
+* With language servers in mind, we designed the [Agent Host Protocol (AHP)](https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/) to allow any client to interact with agent sessions. All of sudden, session continuity across VS Code, Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot App, and github.com lets you pick up right where you left off.
+
+* The Agents window lets you manage your agents across workspaces and environments from a single interface, whether you kick off things yourself or use [automations](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/automations) to handle repetitive tasks.
+
+* By default, agents are now powered by the [Copilot harness](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses), the same harness used in Copilot Code Review, the Copilot CLI, the Copilot App, and Copilot Cloud sessions. Write agent customizations once and use them consistently across all these experiences.
+
+* If you prefer [Anthropic's Claude Code harness or the one from OpenAI Codex](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/agent-harnesses?id=requirements-and-setup), just use those instead with your Copilot subscription and enjoy the familiar VS Code developer experience.
+
+* As we continue to offer new models from different providers, how do you decide which one is best suited for your task? With [model comparisons](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/compare-models) (aka Agent Bake-Off), run the same prompt against multiple models and harnesses to see which performs best. Prefer a hands-off approach? Use [Copilot Fusion](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/concepts/language-models#_copilot-fusion) to choose the best model and orchestrate multiple models to work together for your task.
+
+* We've had vision capabilities for a while, but you kept asking for more. The wait is over, and now you can also prompt the agent to [generate images](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/chat/chat-overview#_generate-and-edit-images-experimental) directly in chat.
+
+* Chat is not always the best interface for every task. With [canvas support](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/canvases), you can create rich, interactive UI to interact with your agents and visualize their outputs.
+
+* Coding with agents can be more than just writing code. Let agents interact with the browser to validate their results, or let them [drive apps on your computer](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/tools#_control-desktop-applications-experimental) for automation and task execution.
+
+* If you need it, build it! So, we created a beautiful new [Markdown editor](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/languages/markdown#_markdown-editor). Instead of editing the raw Markdown, you can edit the rendered Markdown directly. And, of course, you can still edit the source if you prefer.
+
+* And if you didn't notice, we also [refreshed the overall look and feel of VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/blogs/2026/10/15/modern-ui), so it looks fresh and beautiful in light and dark themes.
+
+Read all about this, and more, in our [VS Code Wrapped blog post](https://code.visualstudio.com/blogs/2026/10/28/vscode-wrapped).
+
+## Release highlights
+
+This release helps you keep agent work moving across environments, find the right models for each task, and stay in control of changes and tool calls.
+
+* [Session continuity](#session-continuity): Manage remotes in one place and keep sessions and automations running even when your computer is off.
+
+* [Copilot Fusion and model comparisons](#models): Let Copilot choose and orchestrate models, or compare models side by side.
+
+* [Image generation (Preview)](#image-generation-in-copilot-preview): Create and edit images directly in chat.
+
+* [Computer use (Experimental)](#let-agents-use-desktop-apps-with-computer-use): Let agents use desktop apps on your computer.
+
+* [Working set (Experimental)](#review-copilot-file-edits-with-the-working-set-experimental): Keep or undo agent file edits in the editor.
+
+* [Assisted permissions](#assisted-permissions-are-generally-available): Reduce interruptions with automatic approval for tool calls that pass a risk check.
+
+* [Customization marketplace](#discover-marketplace-customizations-preview) and [Copilot connectors](#connect-services-with-copilot-connectors-preview) (Preview): Discover skills and plugins for your workflow, and bring context from Slack, Notion, and other services into your agent sessions.
+
+## Session continuity
+
+### Run and continue Copilot tasks in the cloud
+
+Cloud sessions let you run Copilot tasks from VS Code without keeping your development machine online. Your repository and tools run in a managed environment on GitHub's infrastructure.
+
+From the **Chat view** in the editor window or the **Agents window**, you can:
+
+* Select **Cloud** and choose a GitHub repository to start a task.
+* Send follow-up instructions, respond to approval requests, and review the agent's changes.
+* Reopen an existing cloud session from the sessions list to continue the same conversation.
+
+Your cloud sessions are also accessible from other Copilot clients. For example, you can check progress on GitHub.com or in the **GitHub Mobile app**, then return to VS Code to continue working.
+
+<video src="images/1_144/cloud-continuity.mp4" title="Video showing cloud continuity in Copilot tasks." autoplay loop controls muted></video>
+
+Cloud sessions use a separate workspace. Local uncommitted changes aren't automatically copied. The new cloud experience requires a paid Copilot plan and is subject to organization policies.
+
+### Manage remote environments
+
+VS Code lets you run agents and perform development tasks across different (remote) environments. To make it easier to manage these environments, we're introducing the **Remote Environments** dialog, which brings your GitHub Environments, Dev Tunnels, WSL distributions, and SSH hosts together in one place.
+
+Select **Manage Remote Environments** at the bottom of the Environment picker to see the status of each remote, connect or disconnect, and choose which remotes should be visible in the pickers.
+
+![Screenshot showing the Remote Environments dialog with GitHub Environments, Dev Tunnels, WSL, and SSH groups, each remote's status, and inline actions for a connected tunnel.](images/1_144/remote-environments.webp)
+
+Learn more about [remote agent sessions](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/remote-agent-sessions).
+
+### Cloud Automations (Preview)
+
+**Setting:** ``chat.automations.cloud.enabled``
+
+Create and manage Copilot cloud automations directly in the Agents window. Enabled by default, they run on GitHub infrastructure on a schedule or in response to repository events, even when your computer is off.
+
+To create a cloud automation, you can ask an agent to set one up for you, or use the **Create Automation** button in the Automations view in the Agents window.
+
+With cloud automations, you can:
+
+* **Set up automations that run in response to issue or pull request events**: Act automatically when activity happens in your repository. For example, automatically triaging issues as they get assigned to you.
+* **Build shared workflows in the cloud with your team**: Create automations that are visible to everyone with access to the repository and act as Copilot.
+* **Control exactly when your agent runs and what it can do**: Limit allowed tools and add filters for precise control over your automations. For example, trigger an automation when you are assigned an issue with a specific label.
+
+![Screenshot showing the create cloud automation interface.](images/1_144/cloud-automations.webp)
+
+To learn more, see [Create and manage agent automations](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/automations) in the Visual Studio Code docs.
+
+### Agent Host Protocol v1.0
+
+We've published the first version of the [Agent Host Protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/), the protocol that VS Code uses to communicate with its agents locally and on remote machines, including for [cloud automations](#cloud-automations-preview). It's an open, extensible protocol designed to be an easy way to build custom UI's for your agents, or build agent platforms that plug into any UI that speaks it.
+
+You can add a websocket-based agent host to your VS Code instance via the command **Agents: Add Remote Agent Host...** in the Agents window, and run `code agent endpoints` to get the endpoints for your editor's running agent host. We publish libraries in six languages and have found agents are good at making clients and hosts using them.
+
+You can read more about the protocol and find additional resources on the [Agent Host Protocol website](https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/).
+
+## Models
+
+### Route and orchestrate models with GitHub Copilot Fusion
+
+Instead of picking a model for each task, select **Copilot Fusion** in the model picker and let Copilot intelligently route requests and orchestrate models for you. Copilot Fusion brings together [Project HydraFusion](https://github.blog/ai-and-ml/github-copilot/project-hydrafusion-frontier-quality-via-multi-model-orchestration/)'s multi-model orchestration and [Copilot auto model selection](https://docs.github.com/copilot/concepts/models/auto-model-selection)'s task-aware model selection to balance performance and cost efficiency.
+
+For each request, Copilot Fusion chooses the models, reasoning effort, and execution pattern for your task. For example, one model completes a simple task, while for harder tasks one model drafts a solution and other models review or critique it. Hover over the effort level below a response to see which models were used.
+
+Choose an effort level to balance quality and cost: **Standard** for everyday coding work, **High** for more demanding tasks, and **Max** for the most complex tasks.
+
+<video src="images/1_144/copilot-fusion.mp4" title="Video showing the model picker in Copilot Chat." autoplay loop controls muted></video>
```

@@ -91,6 +91,274 @@
 
 By default, this file is located at `~/.copilot/providers.json`. Override its location with the `COPILOT_PROVIDERS_CONFIG` environment variable.
 
+Models in this file are available alongside the models provided by your Copilot subscription. After editing the file manually, restart Copilot CLI to load your changes. For setup instructions, see [Add Llm Models](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-llm-models).
+
+> [!WARNING]
+> API keys, bearer tokens, and header values in this file are stored as plain text. Do not commit the file to a repository or share it without removing credentials. Values such as `$MY_API_KEY` are literal strings, not references to environment variables.
+
+#### Provider configuration structure
+
+Use a JSON object, without comments or trailing commas. The file contains two arrays. Each provider defines a connection, and each model refers to one of those providers by name. In the tables below, `[]` means an entry in an array. For example, `models[].capabilities.supports.vision` is the `vision` setting inside `supports`, inside `capabilities`, inside a model entry.
+
+| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
+|-------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
+| `providers` | Array of objects | No | `[]` | Provider connections. See [Provider settings](#provider-settings). |
+| `models` | Array of objects | No | `[]` | Models available through those connections. See [Model settings](#model-settings). |
+
+An absent or empty file, or a file with no provider or model entries, allows the CLI to fall back to `COPILOT_PROVIDER_*` environment variables. A `null` value for either array is treated as an empty array. A file with invalid JSON or invalid provider or model entries produces a configuration error instead.
+
+To use a configured model when starting the CLI, pass `PROVIDER-NAME/MODEL-ID` to the `--model` option. `PROVIDER-NAME` is the provider's `name` value, and `MODEL-ID` is the model's `id` value. For example, run `copilot --model local/qwen3:8b`. Alternatively, during an interactive session, you can enter `/model` and choose the model from the picker.
+
+This file configures connections, model capabilities, and model instructions for use in Copilot CLI. The JSON in this file is not a provider API request body. Settings are not passed through to the provider when you add them to this file.
+
+#### Provider settings
+
+Each entry in `providers` accepts the following fields. Only `name` and `baseUrl` are always required. Authentication requirements depend on the provider.
+
+| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
+|-------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
+| `providers[].name` | String | Yes | None | A unique name for this connection, such as `"local"` or `"my-anthropic"`. Must not contain `/`. Models refer to this name using their `provider` field. |
+| `providers[].type` | String | No | `"openai"` | The connection type: `"openai"` for OpenAI-compatible APIs, `"azure"` for Azure OpenAI, `"anthropic"` for Anthropic's Messages API, or `"local_model"` for a local model served by `llama-server`. |
+| `providers[].baseUrl` | String containing a URL or file path | Yes | None | The provider's API base URL. For OpenAI-compatible APIs, include the required API prefix, such as `https://api.openai.com/v1` or `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` for Ollama. For direct Anthropic access, use `https://api.anthropic.com`. For Azure, use your resource endpoint. With `"type": "local_model"`, this can instead be a path to a `.gguf` model file. |
+| `providers[].wireApi` | String | No | `"completions"` | The API format for OpenAI and Azure connections: `"completions"` for Chat Completions or `"responses"` for the Responses API. Ignored for Anthropic. |
+| `providers[].transport` | String | No | `"http"` | Accepts `"http"` or `"websockets"`. WebSockets require `"type": "openai"` and `"wireApi": "responses"`, and the provider must support that transport. |
+| `providers[].apiKey` | String | Provider-dependent | Unset | The provider's API key. Can be omitted for an unauthenticated local server. |
+| `providers[].bearerToken` | String | Provider-dependent | Unset | A bearer token, without the `Bearer ` prefix. Takes precedence over `apiKey` when both are set. This is a static token, not a token-refresh command. |
+| `providers[].headers` | Object | No | Unset | Additional HTTP headers, with header names as keys and strings as values. |
+| `providers[].headers.<header-name>` | String | No | Unset | The value of a header, for example `"X-Project": "my-project"`. Use `apiKey` or `bearerToken` for standard provider authentication. |
+| `providers[].azure` | Object | No | Unset | Azure-specific options. Contains the `apiVersion` field described below. |
+| `providers[].azure.apiVersion` | String | No | Unset | The Azure API version to request. When set to a non-empty version string supported by your endpoint, the CLI uses the versioned deployment API. When omitted, the CLI uses the versionless `/openai/v1` API. |
+| `providers[].localModel` | Object | No | Unset | Server options for a CLI-managed `.gguf` model. See [Local model server settings](#local-model-server-settings). |
+| `providers[].modelProvider` | String | No | Inferred from the connection | A provider label used only for telemetry. Recognized values are `"openai"`, `"anthropic"`, `"azure_openai"`, `"ollama"`, `"lm_studio"`, `"foundry_local"`, and `"llama_cpp"`. Does not change the connection protocol or model behavior. |
+| `providers[].hasBearerTokenProvider` | Boolean | No | `false` | Indicates that an application using the SDK supplies tokens through a callback. Omit this when configuring the CLI manually. Setting it to `true` in this file does not register a token provider. |
+
+The named-provider file does not support `apiKeyCommand`. Do not put credentials or token-refresh commands in `metadata` or `localModel.args`.
+
+#### Local model server settings
+
+These settings apply only when `providers[].type` is `"local_model"` and `baseUrl` is a path to a `.gguf` file. The CLI starts `llama-server` when the model is first used. The executable must be installed and available on `PATH`. Use an absolute model path to avoid depending on the directory from which you start the CLI.
+
+If `baseUrl` is an HTTP or HTTPS URL, the CLI connects to that existing server and does not use these startup settings. They also do not configure Ollama or other OpenAI-compatible servers.
+
+All fields inside `providers[].localModel` are optional.
+
+| Field | Type | Default | Description |
+|-------|------|---------|-------------|
+| `providers[].localModel.ctxSize` | Non-negative integer | `llama-server` default | Requested context size in tokens, passed as `--ctx-size`. The actual allocation can be smaller than requested. |
+| `providers[].localModel.nGpuLayers` | Non-negative integer | `llama-server` default | Number of model layers to offload to the GPU, passed as `--n-gpu-layers`. |
+| `providers[].localModel.parallel` | Non-negative integer | `1` | Number of server slots, passed as `--parallel`. Multiple slots can divide the available context between requests. |
+| `providers[].localModel.args` | Array of strings | `[]` | Additional `llama-server` arguments. Each argument is a separate string, such as `["--threads", "8"]`. These follow the arguments generated from the fields above. |
+| `providers[].localModel.persist` | Boolean | `false` | Requests that the managed server remain running after a clean CLI exit so a later CLI process can reuse it. Otherwise, the CLI cleans up the server on exit. |
+| `providers[].localModel.logs` | String containing a file path or `"inherit"` | Output discarded | Appends the server's standard output and error output to the specified file. Use an absolute path. `"inherit"` sends output to the terminal and can interfere with the CLI display. |
+
+The CLI manages the server's model path, host, and port. You cannot pass `--model`, `-m`, `--host`, or `--port` through `args`, including forms such as `--port=8080`.
+
+#### Model settings
+
+Each entry in `models` accepts the following fields. Only `id` and `provider` are required.
+
+| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
+|-------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
+| `models[].id` | String | Yes | None | The model identifier used in the CLI. Must be unique within its provider. Also used as the provider's model name unless `wireModel` is set. |
+| `models[].provider` | String | Yes | None | Must match the `name` of an entry in `providers`. |
+| `models[].wireModel` | String | No | Value of `id` | The model or deployment name sent to the provider. Use this when the provider expects a different name from the ID you want to select in the CLI. |
+| `models[].modelId` | String | No | Value of `id` | The model identity used to look up the CLI's model-specific behavior and defaults. For an alias or deployment name, set this to the underlying model's recognized ID. This does not change the model name sent to the provider. |
+| `models[].name` | String | No | `PROVIDER-NAME/MODEL-ID` | A display name for the model. Does not change its selection ID. |
+| `models[].maxPromptTokens` | Integer | No | Model-dependent, otherwise `128000` | The input token budget. Use a positive whole number that matches your model and deployment. |
+| `models[].maxContextWindowTokens` | Integer | No | Known model limit, otherwise unset | The total context-window limit, including input and output tokens. Set this for models whose limit the CLI does not know. |
+| `models[].maxOutputTokens` | Integer | No | Model- and provider-dependent | The output token budget. The provider and the model's reasoning requirements can further constrain the output. |
+| `models[].capabilities` | Object | No | Model defaults | Describes supported features and limits. See [Model capabilities](#model-capabilities). |
+| `models[].systemMessage` | Object | No | Standard CLI instructions | Adds to, replaces, or customizes the system instructions for this model. See [Model system messages](#model-system-messages). |
+| `models[].metadata` | Object | No | Unset | Additional descriptive data, including information saved when a model is discovered. See [Model metadata](#model-metadata). |
+
+The three token-limit fields accept whole numbers from `0` to `4294967295`. Use positive values appropriate for your deployment rather than relying on `0` as a way to disable a limit. These settings tell the CLI what limits to use, but do not increase the model's actual capacity.
+
+#### Model capabilities
+
+The `models[].capabilities` object describes the model. Setting a feature to `true` does not add that feature to a model that does not support it.
+
+| Field | Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-------------|
+| `models[].capabilities.family` | String | Descriptive model-family identifier. Use `modelId`, not this field, to choose the CLI's model-specific behavior. |
+| `models[].capabilities.supports` | Object | Supported features. See [Supported model features](#supported-model-features). |
+| `models[].capabilities.limits` | Object | Token and image limits. See [Model capability limits](#model-capability-limits). |
+
+All capability fields are optional. Objects are merged with the model's defaults, and arrays replace the corresponding default arrays.
+
+#### Supported model features
+
+The following fields belong inside `models[].capabilities.supports`.
+
+| Field | Type | Description |
+|-------|------|-------------|
+| `models[].capabilities.supports.vision` | Boolean | Whether the model accepts images. Defaults to `false` when no other capability information is available. |
+| `models[].capabilities.supports.toolCalls` | Boolean | Whether the model supports tool calls. The spelling `tool_calls` is also accepted and takes precedence if both are present. This describes support, not permission to run tools. |
+| `models[].capabilities.supports.streaming` | Boolean | Whether the model supports streamed responses. This is capability information, not a setting to turn response streaming on or off. |
+| `models[].capabilities.supports.adaptive_thinking` | String or boolean | The model's support for Anthropic adaptive thinking. Prefer one of the string values described below. For compatibility, `true` means `"optional"` and `false` means `"unsupported"`. |
+| `models[].capabilities.supports.reasoning_effort` | Array of strings | Reasoning-effort levels the model supports. This advertises available levels, not the level to use for a request. The CLI also applies model-specific restrictions. |
+| `models[].capabilities.supports.thinking` | Boolean | Descriptive support information that model discovery can save. Does not by itself configure thinking or enable reasoning-effort controls. |
+| `models[].capabilities.supports.reasoningEffort` | Boolean or array of strings | Compatibility field. A boolean does not enable reasoning-effort controls, and an array is not used consistently across CLI features. Use `reasoning_effort` for a supported-level list. |
+
+The `adaptive_thinking` values have the following meanings.
+
+| Value | Meaning |
+|-------|---------|
+| `"unsupported"` | The model does not support adaptive thinking. This does not rule out other forms of reasoning. |
+| `"optional"` | The model supports adaptive thinking, but does not require it. |
```

 Each `--json` entry has the shape `{ id, fileExtensions?, sourcePlugin? }`.
 
 Custom agents and session-scoped hooks aren't covered by `copilot instruction`, `copilot lsp`, `copilot plugin`, `copilot mcp`, or `copilot skill`. All require a live session.
+
+### Importing memories
+
+Use `copilot memories import` to validate and import user-level preferences and repository-level facts from a JSONL file.
+
+```shell
+copilot memories import PATH-TO-FILE
+```
+
+| Option | Description |
+| --- | --- |
+| `--dry-run` | Validate the complete file without authenticating or submitting memories. |
+| `--on-conflict skip\|error` | Skip conflicting records or treat them as errors. The default is `error`. |
+| `--output json` | Return the import result as JSON instead of human-readable text. |
+
+If any line fails schema validation, no records are submitted. After validation succeeds, records are submitted individually, so a service failure can result in a partial import. Check the per-record results and retry only failed records. The `--on-conflict skip` option skips duplicate IDs within the input file and conflicts reported by the memory service. It does not guarantee that repeating an import will avoid duplicate memories. For the file format and examples, see [Create Memories](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/use-copilot-agents/copilot-memory/create-memories#importing-memories-with-copilot-cli).

Isolated to the default agent’s tool schemas, total description tokens drop `,_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`43%`}),` (4,005 → 2,302); combined with the empty base prompt and opt-in todos, a default-agent turn’s input tokens drop `,_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`65%`}),` (5,395 → 1,895). Tool behavior is unchanged. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4859`,children:`#4859`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4979`,children:`#4979`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/5009`,children:`#5009`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`features-3`,children:`Features`}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/customization#middleware`,children:`Override a default middleware instance`})}),`: A `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware=`}),` (or subagent `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware`}),`) instance whose `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`.name`}),` matches a built-in now replaces that default in place, rather than erroring on a duplicate. For example, pass your own `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`SummarizationMiddleware(...)`}),` to change the token trigger or summary model without disabling the built-in default. `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`write_file`}),` now overwrites an existing file instead of erroring (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4109`,children:`#4109`}),`); and reads and searches are tuned for open models — paginated `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`read_file`}),` reports total and remaining lines plus the next `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`offset`}),` (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4540`,children:`#4540`}),`), `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`grep`}),`/`,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`glob`}),` return partial results with a `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`truncated`}),` flag instead of hanging on large trees (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4063`,children:`#4063`}),`), and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`grep`}),` gains a 1,000-match cap with streamed output and optional context lines (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4570`,children:`#4570`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4706`,children:`#4706`}),`).`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`More prompt-caching support`}),`: Bedrock prompt caching via the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents[aws]`}),` extra (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/issues/4108`,children:`#4108`}),`), and automatic Fireworks prompt-cache session affinity (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4598`,children:`#4598`}),`).`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`NVIDIA support`}),`: A built-in Nemotron 3 Ultra harness profile plus NIM app-origin attribution. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4561`,children:`#4561`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(_components.p,{children:`Copy the following prompt into your AI coding assistant to migrate a codebase for these breaking changes:`}),_jsx(Prompt,{description:`Migrate a deepagents codebase from v0.6.x to v0.7.`,icon:`arrow-right`,actions:[`copy`],children:'Migrate this codebase from `deepagents` v0.6.x to v0.7 to account for the following breaking changes:\\n\\n1. `create_deep_agent` no longer includes `TodoListMiddleware` by default. If this codebase relies on the `write_todos` tool, the `todos` state channel, or the todo-planning prompt, restore it by importing `TodoListMiddleware` from `langchain.agents.middleware` (not `deepagents`) and passing it to `create_deep_agent`:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from langchain.agents.middleware import TodoListMiddleware\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()])\\n   ```\\n\\n2. Backend compatibility shims were removed: `BackendFactory`, `BACKEND_TYPES`, `FileFormat`, and `Unset` no longer exist. Replace any backend factories with concrete `BackendProtocol` instances, and add an explicit `namespace` to every `StoreBackend` configuration:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n   from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\\n\\n   # Before (v0.6.x): factory callable, and StoreBackend with no explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend())  # [!code --]\\n\\n   # After (v0.7): concrete backend instance with an explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)))  # [!code ++]\\n   ```\\n\\n   Also update calls to use the current `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, and `ReadResult` APIs.\\n\\n3. Tool output formats changed: empty `ls` / `glob` output is now the string `No files found` instead of `[]`, and `read_file` no longer renders a fixed-width `cat -n`-style line-number gutter. Tool behavior is unchanged. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4859`,children:`#4859`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4979`,children:`#4979`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/5009`,children:`#5009`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`features-3`,children:`Features`}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/customization#middleware`,children:`Override a default middleware instance`})}),`: A `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware=`}),` (or subagent `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware`}),`) instance whose `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`.name`}),` matches a built-in now replaces that default in place, rather than erroring on a duplicate. For example, pass your own `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`SummarizationMiddleware(...)`}),` to change the token trigger or summary model without disabling the built-in default. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4251`,children:`#4251`}),`)`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Filesystem tools`}),`: New `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/tools#built-in-harness-tools`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`delete`})}),` tool removes a file or recursively removes a directory (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/3659`,children:`#3659`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/3851`,children:`#3851`}),`); `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`write_file`}),` now overwrites an existing file instead of erroring (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4109`,children:`#4109`}),`); `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`FilesystemMiddleware`}),` accepts a `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/overview#virtual-filesystem-access`,children:`tool allowlist`}),` to expose only selected built-in tools (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4325`,children:`#4325`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4698`,children:`#4698`}),`); (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4561`,children:`#4561`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(_components.p,{children:`Copy the following prompt into your AI coding assistant to migrate a codebase for these breaking changes:`}),_jsx(Prompt,{description:`Migrate a deepagents codebase from v0.6.x to v0.7.`,icon:`arrow-right`,actions:[`copy`],children:'Migrate this codebase from `deepagents` v0.6.x to v0.7 to account for the following breaking changes:\\n\\n1. `create_deep_agent` no longer includes `TodoListMiddleware` by default. If this codebase relies on the `write_todos` tool, the `todos` state channel, or the todo-planning prompt, restore it by importing `TodoListMiddleware` from `langchain.agents.middleware` (not `deepagents`) and passing it to `create_deep_agent`:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from langchain.agents.middleware import TodoListMiddleware\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()])\\n   ```\\n\\n2. Backend compatibility shims were removed: `BackendFactory`, `BACKEND_TYPES`, `FileFormat`, and `Unset` no longer exist. Replace any backend factories with concrete `BackendProtocol` instances, and add an explicit `namespace` to every `StoreBackend` configuration:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n   from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\\n\\n   # Before (v0.6.x): factory callable, and StoreBackend with no explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend())  # [!code --]\\n\\n   # After (v0.7): concrete backend instance with an explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)))  # [!code ++]\\n   ```\\n\\n   Also update calls to use the current `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, and `ReadResult` APIs.\\n\\n3. Tool output formats changed: empty `ls` / `glob` output is now the string `No files found` instead of `[]`, and `read_file` no longer renders a fixed-width `cat -n`-style line-number gutter. Update any code that parses these tool outputs.\\n\\nSearch the codebase for usages of the removed symbols and for parsing logic that depends on the old output formats, apply the necessary changes, and flag anything that needs manual review.\\n'})]}),`\n`,_jsxs(Update,{label:`May 12, 2026`,tags:[`deepagents`],rss:{title:`May 12, 2026 - langchain`},id:`may-12%2C-2026`,children:[_jsxs(Heading,{level:`2`,id:`deepagents-v0-6-0`,children:[_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents`}),` v0.6.0`]}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/interpreters`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CodeInterpreterMiddleware`})})}),`: (experimental) `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents`}),` now supports code execution and programmatic tool calling through a scoped QuickJS runtime.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[`Supports `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`version=\"v3\"`}),` in `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`stream_events`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`astream_events`}),`. Downgrading to an earlier Deep Agents version switches these channels back to non-delta channels, leaving existing delta checkpoints unreadable and causing incomplete or incorrect state reconstruction. More generally, avoid switching a persisted channel between delta and non-delta representations. If this codebase relies on the `write_todos` tool, the `todos` state channel, or the todo-planning prompt, restore it by importing `TodoListMiddleware` from `langchain.agents.middleware` (not `deepagents`) and passing it to `create_deep_agent`:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from langchain.agents.middleware import TodoListMiddleware\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()])\\n   ```\\n\\n2. Backend compatibility shims were removed: `BackendFactory`, `BACKEND_TYPES`, `FileFormat`, and `Unset` no longer exist. Replace any backend factories with concrete `BackendProtocol` instances, and add an explicit `namespace` to every `StoreBackend` configuration:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n   from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\\n\\n   # Before (v0.6.x): factory callable, and StoreBackend with no explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend())  # [!code --]\\n\\n   # After (v0.7): concrete backend instance with an explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)))  # [!code ++]\\n   ```\\n\\n   Also update calls to use the current `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, and `ReadResult` APIs.\\n\\n3. Tool output formats changed: empty `ls` / `glob` output is now the string `No files found` instead of `[]`, and `read_file` no longer renders a fixed-width `cat -n`-style line-number gutter. Tool behavior is unchanged. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4859`,children:`#4859`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4979`,children:`#4979`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/5009`,children:`#5009`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`features-3`,children:`Features`}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/customization#middleware`,children:`Override a default middleware instance`})}),`: A `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware=`}),` (or subagent `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware`}),`) instance whose `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`.name`}),` matches a built-in now replaces that default in place, rather than erroring on a duplicate. For example, pass your own `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`SummarizationMiddleware(...)`}),` to change the token trigger or summary model without disabling the built-in default. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4251`,children:`#4251`}),`)`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Filesystem tools`}),`: New `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/tools#built-in-harness-tools`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`delete`})}),` tool removes a file or recursively removes a directory (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/3659`,children:`#3659`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/3851`,children:`#3851`}),`); (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4561`,children:`#4561`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(_components.p,{children:`Copy the following prompt into your AI coding assistant to migrate a codebase for these breaking changes:`}),_jsx(Prompt,{description:`Migrate a deepagents codebase from v0.6.x to v0.7.`,icon:`arrow-right`,actions:[`copy`],children:'Migrate this codebase from `deepagents` v0.6.x to v0.7 to account for the following breaking changes:\\n\\n1. `create_deep_agent` no longer includes `TodoListMiddleware` by default. If this codebase relies on the `write_todos` tool, the `todos` state channel, or the todo-planning prompt, restore it by importing `TodoListMiddleware` from `langchain.agents.middleware` (not `deepagents`) and passing it to `create_deep_agent`:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from langchain.agents.middleware import TodoListMiddleware\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()])\\n   ```\\n\\n2. Backend compatibility shims were removed: `BackendFactory`, `BACKEND_TYPES`, `FileFormat`, and `Unset` no longer exist. Replace any backend factories with concrete `BackendProtocol` instances, and add an explicit `namespace` to every `StoreBackend` configuration:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n   from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\\n\\n   # Before (v0.6.x): factory callable, and StoreBackend with no explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend())  # [!code --]\\n\\n   # After (v0.7): concrete backend instance with an explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)))  # [!code ++]\\n   ```\\n\\n   Also update calls to use the current `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, and `ReadResult` APIs.\\n\\n3. Tool output formats changed: empty `ls` / `glob` output is now the string `No files found` instead of `[]`, and `read_file` no longer renders a fixed-width `cat -n`-style line-number gutter. Update any code that parses these tool outputs.\\n\\nSearch the codebase for usages of the removed symbols and for parsing logic that depends on the old output formats, apply the necessary changes, and flag anything that needs manual review.\\n'})]}),`\n`,_jsxs(Update,{label:`May 12, 2026`,tags:[`deepagents`],rss:{title:`May 12, 2026 - langchain`},id:`may-12%2C-2026`,children:[_jsxs(Heading,{level:`2`,id:`deepagents-v0-6-0`,children:[_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents`}),` v0.6.0`]}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/interpreters`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`CodeInterpreterMiddleware`})})}),`: (experimental) `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents`}),` now supports code execution and programmatic tool calling through a scoped QuickJS runtime.`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[`Supports `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`version=\"v3\"`}),` in `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`stream_events`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`astream_events`}),`. Rather than re-serializing the full accumulated value into every checkpoint, only the incremental delta written at each step is stored — keeping checkpoint sizes small as threads grow long.`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(Warning,{children:_jsxs(_components.p,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Rolling back from v0.6.0 is not supported once threads have persisted.`}),` Deep Agents v0.6.0 changes persisted message history and agent files to `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`DeltaChannel`}),`, which writes checkpoints in a new format that earlier versions cannot read. Downgrading to an earlier Deep Agents version switches these channels back to non-delta channels, leaving existing delta checkpoints unreadable and causing incomplete or incorrect state reconstruction. If you need to roll back, use the `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/tree/main/examples/delta-channel-dump`,children:`delta-channel-dump recovery script`}),` to migrate affected threads, or discard them, before downgrading.
